2. Airworthiness Limitation Precautions
A. General
(1) Critical Design Configuration Control Limitations (CDCCLs)
(a) All occurrences of CDCCLs found in this chapter of the AMM are identified by this note
after each applicable CDCCL design feature:
1) NOTE: CDCCL - Refer to the task: Airworthiness Limitation Precautions,
TASK 29-00-00-910-801, for important information on Critical Design Configuration
Control Limitations (CDCCLs).
(b) Design features that are CDCCLs are defined and controlled by Special Federal Aviation
Regulation (SFAR) 88, and can be found in Section 9 of the Maintenance Planning Data
(MPD) document. CDCCLs are a means of identifying certain design configuration
features intended to preclude a fuel tank ignition source for the operational life of the
airplane. CDCCLs are mandatory and cannot be changed or deleted without the approval
of the FAA Oversight Office that is responsible for the airplane model Type Certificate. A
critical fuel tank ignition source prevention feature may exist in the fuel system and its
related installation or in systems that, if a failure condition were to develop, could interact
with the fuel system in such a way that an unsafe condition would develop without this
limitation. Strict adherence to configuration, methods, techniques, and practices as
prescribed is required to ensure the CDCCL is complied with. Any use of parts, methods,
techniques or practices not contained in the applicable CDCCL must be approved by the
FAA Oversight Office that is responsible for the airplane model Type Certificate.
(2) Airworthiness Limitation Instructions (ALIs)
(a) All occurrences of fuel tank system ALIs found in this chapter of the AMM are identified
by this note after each applicable ALI inspection feature:
1) NOTE: ALI - Refer to the task: Airworthiness Limitation Precautions,
TASK 29-00-00-910-801, for important information on airworthiness limitation
instructions (ALIs).
29-00-00
(b) Inspection features that are ALIs are defined and controlled by Special Federal Aviation
Regulation (SFAR) 88, and can be found in Section 9 of the Maintenance Planning Data
(MPD) document. These ALIs identify inspection features related to fuel tank ignition
source prevention which must be done to maintain the design level of safety for the
operational life of the airplane. These inspection features are mandatory and cannot be
changed or deleted without the approval of the FAA Oversight Office that is responsible
for the airplane model Type Certificate. Strict adherence to methods, techniques and
practices as prescribed is required to ensure the ALI is complied with. Any use of
methods, techniques or practices not contained in these ALIs must be approved by the
FAA Oversight Office that is responsible for the airplane model Type Certificate.

F . Prepare to Replace the Hydraulic Fluid
SUBTASK 29-00-00-100-001
(1) During this replacement, if hydraulic fluid gets on the airplane, do this task: Clean (Wet Wash)
the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean (Waterless Wash) the
External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-803.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-860-001
(2) Make sure that hydraulic power is removed from the A and B hydraulic systems
(TASK 29-11-00-860-805).
SUBTASK 29-00-00-860-284
(3) Make sure that hydraulic power is removed from the standby hydraulic system
(TASK 29-21-00-000-802).
SUBTASK 29-00-00-860-002
(4) Release the pressure from the hydraulic reservoirs (TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or
TASK 29-09-00-860-808).
RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 PRE SB 737-29-1106
SUBTASK 29-00-00-480-001
(5) Install the lockset, SPL-1795, on the systems A and B depressurization (vent) valves when the
valves are fully open.
RYR ALL
SUBTASK 29-00-00-680-001
(6) Drain the hydraulic fluid from the system A and B hydraulic reservoirs into a 50 Gallon (190 l)
hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-3901.
(a) Remove the lockwire or safety cable from the handle of the applicable reservoir drain
valve.
NOTE: Do this with the drain valve that is on the bottom of each reservoir.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-420-001
(7) Close the drain valves.
(a) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51674, on the handle of the
reservoir drain valve with double twist method.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-616-002
(8) Drain the hydraulic fluid from the standby hydraulic system as follows:
(a) Do the steps of either Method 1 or Method 2 to drain the hydraulic fluid from the standby
system reservoir:
1) Do these steps to accomplish Method 1:
29-00-00
CAUTION
PULL DOWN ON THE KNURLED RING OF THE SELF-SEAL
DISCONNECT BEFORE YOU TURN IT . IF YOU DO NOT DO
THIS, TOO MUCH TORQUE WILL BE NECESSARY TO TURN
THE RING. THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SELF-SEAL
DISCONNECT .
a) Disconnect the supply line for the standby hydraulic pump at the
quick-disconnect on the bottom of the standby hydraulic reservoir.
b) Connect a drain hose, SPL-6107, to the quick-disconnect on the bottom of the
standby reservoir.
c) Put the end of the drain hose, SPL-6107, into a 5 gallon (19 liter) container,
STD-1154.
d) Drain the hydraulic fluid into the 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154.
e) Disconnect the drain hose, SPL-6107, from the quick-disconnect on the
bottom of the standby reservoir.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT
BEFORE YOU INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL
DISCONNECT . IF TOO MUCH TORQUE IS NECESSARY TO DO
THE INSTALLATION, DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL
DISCONNECT AND MAKE SURE THAT THE POPPET IS
STRAIGHT . AFTER THE INSTALLATION, MAKE SURE THAT THE
INDICATOR PINS EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 INCH. IF THE
INDICATOR PINS DO NOT CORRECTLY EXTEND, FLUID FLOW
WILL DECREASE OR STOP . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
THE RESERVOIR OR THE PUMP .
f) Reconnect the supply line for the standby hydraulic pump at the
quick-disconnect on the bottom of the standby hydraulic reservoir.
2) Do these steps to accomplish Method 2:
a) Open this access panel to get access to the standby hydraulic system EMDP:
Number Name/Location
194DR Aft Wing To Body Fairing Panel
b) Put a 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154, below the standby Electric
Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP).
c) Disconnect the supply line at the standby EMDP .
d) Put the disconnected end of the supply line into the 5 gallon (19 liter)
container, STD-1154.
e) Allow the hydraulic fluid from the standby reservoir to drain into the 5 gallon
(19 liter) container, STD-1154.
f) Reconnect the supply line to the standby EMDP .
g) Close this access panel:
Number Name/Location
194DR Aft Wing To Body Fairing Panel
(b) Drain the hydraulic fluid collected from the standby hydraulic reservoir into a 50 Gallon
(190 l) hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-3901.

H. System A Hydraulic Fluid Replacement
SUBTASK 29-00-00-580-001
(1) Do this task: Lift the Airplane with the Jacks, TASK 07-11-01-580-815.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-480-006
(2) Connect the pressure line of the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163, to the pressure line of the
system A EDP with hydraulic fitting union, STD-15053.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-860-008
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM ALL CONTROL SURFACES
AND THE NOSE GEAR WHEN HYDRAULIC POWER IS SUPPLIED. THE
AILERONS, ELEVATORS, RUDDER, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, AND THE
NOSE GEAR ARE SUPPLIED WITH POWER BY THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEMS.
INJURIES TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR WHEN
HYDRAULIC POWER IS SUPPLIED.
(3) Operate the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163, to pressurize system A to 3000 psi
(20,684 kPa).
SUBTASK 29-00-00-860-009
(4) Retract and extend the main and nose landing gear through one full cycle
(TASK 32-32-00-710-801 and TASK 32-33-00-710-801).
NOTE: Do these at the same time.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-580-003
(5) Do this task: Lower the Airplane Off the Jacks, TASK 07-11-01-580-816.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-860-010
(6) Set the FLT CONTROL A and SPOILER A switches, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the
ON position.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-860-011
(7) Operate the elevators through seven full cycles, from down to up to down.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-860-012
(8) Operate the nose wheel steering through two full cycles (TASK 32-51-00-700-801).
SUBTASK 29-00-00-860-013
(9) Operate the rudders through two full cycles.
29-00-00
SUBTASK 29-00-00-860-014
(10) Set the rudder to the neutral position.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-860-015
(11) Turn the control wheel through five full cycles.
NOTE: This operates the flight spoilers and the ailerons.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-860-016
(12) Set the control wheel to the neutral position.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-860-017
(13) Set the FLT CONTROL A and SPOILER A switches, on the P5 panel, to the OFF position.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-860-018
(14) Operate the thrust reverser of the No. 1 engine through three full cycles
(TASK 78-31-00-980-802-F00 and TASK 78-31-00-980-801-F00).
SUBTASK 29-00-00-860-019
(15) Operate the control lever for the speed brakes through two full cycles.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-870-001
(16) Open the bleed valves on each brake and let a minimum of 2 quarts of fluid bleed from each
brake (TASK 32-41-00-870-803).
SUBTASK 29-00-00-860-020
(17) Remove the pressure from the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-080-004
(18) Disconnect the pressure line of the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163, from the pressure line of
the system A EDP .
SUBTASK 29-00-00-080-005
(19) Disconnect the drain hose from the supply line for the system A EDP .
SUBTASK 29-00-00-611-001
(20) Service the system A hydraulic reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing,
TASK 12-12-00-610-801.

2. Hydraulic System External Leakage Check
(Table 602)
A. General
(1) The table of permitted external leakage gives the maximum external leakage rates for different
parts for normal operation and for dispatch of the airplane to avoid a delay. You must make a
decision on the total leakage you will permit from all of the parts.
(2) It is possible that a crack in a static seal housing can cause a leakage. This leakage can
increase with increased pressure.
(3) Some NAS1611 seals can leak at cold temperatures that occur in flight. If there is evidence of
leakage near one of these seals that cannot be duplicated on the ground, the seal should be
replaced with an improved seal (SL 20-048). Areas where these seals are used include:
(a) Leading edge swivel assembly (if evidence of leakage, replace assembly with improved
seal assembly)
(b) Trailing edge swivel assembly (if evidence of leakage, replace assembly with improved
seal assembly)
(c) Flight control actuators
(d) Brake metering valves
(e) MLG retract actuator
(f) MLG shimmy damper
(g) Standby rudder PCU
(h) Main rudder PCU.
(4) Do a leakage check of these components:
(a) In the wing leading edge and trailing edge area:
1) Tighten tube and fitting connections to the correct torque.
a) Use table 405 in Flareless Tubing Assembly Installation,
TASK 20-10-51-400-804 to find the correct torque values.
b) Replace any tube or fitting connections that continue to leak.
(b) In the rudder and tail area:
1) Tighten tube, hose, and fitting connections to the correct torque.
a) Use table 405 in Flareless Tubing Assembly Installation,
TASK 20-10-51-400-804 to find the correct torque values.
b) Replace any tube, hose, or fitting connections that continue to leak.
(c) Replace these components in the main landing gear wheel well if there is any evidence of
leakage:
1) Hydraulic fuses
2) Cracked hydraulic fittings
3) Loose frangible fittings.
(5) These conditions are important when you do a leakage check for the various components:
(a) The seal at the B-nut tube connections is made by metal-to-metal surfaces. If a leak will
not stop when you tighten the B-nut to the correct torque, the joint is defective and must
be repaired.
29-00-00
(b) Supply hydraulic pressure to the component while you measure the leakage.
(c) If it is possible, operate the actuators to see if the leakage changes during the travel.
(d) Make sure that the leak is not a type which will increase to a much higher rate with time.
Use the type of leak and the length of time the component is pressurized to make this
decision.
(e) Make sure that all the reservoirs are full before each flight.
(f) After each flight, do a check of the components which have a leak.
(g) If hydraulic fluid collects in the area of the leak, it must not cause damage to the airplane
equipment.

NOTE: For the Thrust Reverser actuator leakage limit rate, see

(d) Remove the pressure from the applicable hydraulic system.

*[1] There are approximately 20 drops in a cubic centimeter or 75600 drops in a gallon.
*[2] Airplane can still dispatch if the leakage is above the Normal Limit but under the Dispatch Limit. The intent of this
table specifying Normal Limits and Dispatch Limits are to distinguish the leakage rates that may be allowable for
dispatch to avoid delays, but are not considered normal and maintenance action should be taken. Leakage checks
are recommended after each flight when leakage rates are above Normal Limits but below Dispatch Limits.
*[3] Make sure the connection is tightened to the correct torque.
*[4] Leakage is defined as the escape of fluid from any point of the fitting assembly including the fitting-tube junction,
which returns within a time period after being cleaned up (see *[5]). This junction is defined to include one tube
outside diameter in length beyond the fitting envelope. The fitting envelope is the area from free parent tube material
to free parent tube material or boss.
*[5] Evidence of fluid on a fitting joint does not always indicate a leakage condition. For example, a fitting joint may appear
moist due to: (a) residual assembly lubricant (MCS352); (b) residual fluid from previous leakage that was corrected
but not properly cleaned up or; (c) residual fluid from previous leakage that was corrected and properly cleaned up,
but later drained from an inaccessible area (such as fluid from threads within a flareless joint which does not return
when re-wiped).
*[6] A static seal is a seal between two parts that do not move relative to each other (Example: manifold cover, pump
housing cover).
*[7] Leakage may be checked while the airplane is parked by cycling the landing gear lever with the “A” hydraulic system
pressurized. Make sure the landing gear lock pins are installed before cycling the lever.
*[8] A dynamic seal is a seal between two parts that move relative to each other (Example: piston rod seal, pump shaft
seal, swivel seal).
29-00-00
*[9] The center vent on the rudder PCU is actually the drain for the two dynamic seals. Thus, when evaluating leakage
from the center vent at the rudder PCU, all dynamic seal limits can be doubled.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-360-001
(6) To check the leakage of the Engine Driven Pump (EDP), pressurize the hydraulic system by
doing this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization with an Engine-Driven Pump (EDP),
TASK 29-11-00-860-804.
(a) Stop the applicable engine when the hydraulic power has stabilized at 2800 psig
(19,305 kPa) - 3200 psig (22,063 kPa) (TASK 71-00-00-700-819-F00).
NOTE: This task stops the hydraulic pump but the hydraulic system will remained
pressurized.
(b) Compare the leakage rate of the EDP with the external leakage limits in Table 602.
(c) If the leakage rate is more than the external leakage limits in the table, do the appropriate
tasks to replace the EDP (PAGEBLOCK 29-11-11/401).
(d) To remove the hydraulic fluid from the area of the leakage, do this task: Clean (Wet
Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean
(Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-803.
29-00-00-790-802Gross Internal Leakage CheckPDF p. 76
Open original AMM PDF - page 76 ↗ 
3. Gross Internal Leakage Check
(Figure 601, Figure 602)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) Use this check to find the gross internal leakage of the A and B hydraulic systems.
(2) You must find the changes in the flow of hydraulic fluid (during different conditions of operation)
to find the internal leakage rate for each system. There are three methods to measure the flow:
the ammeter, the flowmeter, and the amp-clamp/multimeter.
(a) To use the ammeter method, you must connect an ammeter in series with one phase of
the motor on the Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP). To find the flow you measure the
current, subtract the other current reading as directed, and use the (Figure 602) to
change it to a flow.
(b) To use the flowmeter method, you install a flowmeter on a hydraulic service cart and read
the flow from it.
(c) To use the amp-clamp/multimeter method, you put the amp-clamp adapter around one of
the wires connected to a relay for the EMDP . You can use either a dedicated amp-clamp
meter or a clamp-on current probe connected to a generic multimeter. You then read the
current directly on the amp-clamp meter or on the multimeter that is connected to the
clamp-on current probe. To find the flow you measure the current, subtract the other
current readings as directed, and use the (Figure 602) to get the flow.
(3) When you read the current, make a record of the value to the nearest 0.1 ampere.
(4) When you read the flowmeter, make a record of the value to the nearest 100 cc/minute.

29-00-00-790-803System A or System B Sub-System Internal Leakage CheckPDF p. 95
Open original AMM PDF - page 95 ↗ 
4. System A or System B Sub-System Internal Leakage Check
(Figure 601, Figure 602)
A. General
(1) Use this check to find the internal leakage of the systems that use hydraulic power.
(2) You must find the changes in the flow of hydraulic fluid (during different conditions of operation)
to find the internal leakage rate for each part of the system. There are three methods to
measure the flow: the ammeter, the flowmeter, and the amp-clamp multimeter.
(a) To use the ammeter method, you connect an ammeter in series with one phase of the
motor on the electric motor-driven pump (EMDP) (Figure 601). To find the flow you
measure the current, subtract the other current readings as directed, and use
(Figure 602) to change it to a flow.
(b) To use the flowmeter method, you install a flowmeter on a hydraulic service cart and read
the flow from it.
(c) To use the amp-clamp/multimeter method, you put the amp-clamp adapter around one of
the wires connected to a relay for the EMDP . You can use either a dedicated amp-clamp
meter or a clamp-on current probe connected to a generic multimeter. You then read the
current directly on the amp-clamp meter or on the multimeter that is connected to the
clamp-on current probe. To find the flow you measure the current, subtract the other
current readings as directed, and use (Figure 602) to get the flow.
(3) When you read the ammeter, make a record of the value to the nearest 0.1 ampere.
(4) When you read the flowmeter, make a record of the value to the nearest 100 cc/minute.

5. Part Internal Leakage Check
(Figure 601, Figure 602)
A. General
(1) Use this check to find the internal leakage of each part or a small group of parts.
(2) To find the condition of the parts of the hydraulic system you compare the leakage you
measured to the maximum leakage. If you find a leakage that is more than the maximum, you
must replace the parts that have too much leakage. Refer to Chapter 27 (Flight Controls),
Chapter 32 (Landing Gear), or Chapter 22 (Autoflight) for the applicable removal and
installation procedures.
(3) You must find the changes in the flow of hydraulic fluid (during different conditions of operation)
to find the internal leakage rate for each part. There are three methods to measure the flow:
the ammeter, the flowmeter, and the amp-clamp multimeter.
(a) To use the ammeter method, you connect an ammeter in series with one phase of the
motor on the electric motor-driven pump (EMDP) (Figure 601). To find the flow you
measure the current subtract the applicable system basic current, and use the
(Figure 602) to change it to a flow.
(b) To use the flowmeter method, you install a flowmeter on a portable hydraulic cart and
read the flow from it.
(c) To use the amp-clamp/multimeter method, put the amp-clamp adapter around one of the
wires connected to a relay for the EMDP . You can use either a dedicated amp-clamp
meter or a clamp-on current probe connected to a generic multimeter. You then read the
current directly on the amp-clamp meter or on the multimeter that is connected to the
clamp-on current probe. To find the flow you measure the current, subtract the other
current readings as directed, and use the (Figure 602) to get the flow.
(4) When you read the ammeter, make a record of the value (on the data sheets in this manual) to
the nearest 0.1 ampere.

6. Standby Hydraulic System Internal Leakage Check
(Figure 603, Figure 604, Figure 605)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) Use this check to find the general internal condition of the standby hydraulic system.
(2) To find the internal leakage of the standby system you will measure the flow (from the standby
Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP)) before and after the standby rudder actuator is in
operation. There are three methods to measure the flow from the standby EMDP: the ammeter,
flowmeter, and amp-clamp multimeter.
NOTE: The standby rudder Power Control Unit (PCU) is the only component that is checked in
this procedure.
(a) To use the ammeter method, you connect an ammeter in series with one phase of the
motor on the standby EMDP (Figure 603). To find the flow you measure the current and
use the (Figure 604) to change it to a flow.
(b) To use the flowmeter method, you install a flowmeter at the outlet of the standby EMDP
and read the flow from it.
29-00-00
(c) To use the amp-clamp multimeter method, you put the amp-clamp adapter around one of
the wires connected to a circuit breaker, pump relay R643, or standby EMDP . You can
use either a dedicated amp-clamp meter or a clamp-on current probe connected to a
generic multimeter. You then read the current directly on the amp-clamp meter or on the
multimeter that is connected to the clamp-on current probe. To find the flow you measure
the current, subtract the other current readings as directed, and use the (Figure 604) to
get the flow.

7. Hydraulic System Elevator, Aileron Power Control Units (PCU's) and Leading Edge Flap and Slat
Actuators Internal Leakage Check
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) This procedure does an internal leakage check for the elevator, aileron power control units and
leading edge flap and slat actuators. The purpose of this leakage test is to identify high
leakage PCU's and actuators it will not identify specific PCU's or actuators for replacement.
(2) Use this check to find the internal leakage of the systems that use hydraulic power.
(3) You must find the changes in the flow of hydraulic fluid (during different conditions of operation)
to find the internal leakage rate for each part. There are three methods to measure the flow:
the ammeter, the flowmeter, and the amp-clamp and multimeter.
(a) To use the ammeter method, you connect an ammeter in series with one phase of the
motor on the electric motor-driven pump (EMDP) (Figure 601). To find the flow you
measure the current subtract the applicable system basic current, and use the
(Figure 602) to change it to a flow.
(b) To use the flowmeter method, you install a flowmeter on a portable hydraulic cart and
read the flow from it.
(c) To use the amp-clamp/multimeter method, you put the amp-clamp adapter around one of
the wires connected to a relay for the EMDP . You can use either a dedicated amp-clamp
meter or a clamp-on current probe connected to a generic multimeter. You then read the
current directly on the amp-clamp meter or on the multimeter that is connected to the
clamp-on current probe. To find the flow you measure the current, subtract the other
current readings as directed, and use the (Figure 602) to get the flow.
(4) When you read the ammeter, make a record of the value (on the data sheets in this manual) to
the nearest 0.1 ampere.
(5) When you read the flowmeter, make a record of the value to the nearest 100 cc/minute.

2. Hydraulic Components - Corrosion Protection
A. References
Reference Title
51-21-91-620-802 Application of Corrosion Inhibiting Compound (P/B 701)
SRM 51-10-02 Structural Repair Manual
B. Consumable Materials
Reference Description Specification
A00767 Sealant - Fuel T ank BMS5-45
B00148 Solvent - Methyl Ethyl Ketone (MEK) ASTM D740
G00009 Compound - Organic Corrosion Inhibiting BMS3-23
G00034 Cotton Wiper - Process Cleaning Absorbent
Wiper (Cheesecloth, Gauze)
AMS3819 Class 1
Grade A or B Form 1
(Supersede BMS15-5
CL A)
C. Hydraulic Lines and Fittings - Corrosion Protection
SUBTASK 29-00-00-916-001
(1) For periodic inspections of the hydraulic lines, do the steps that follow:
(a) Examine the hydraulic lines for signs of corrosion.
NOTE: Corrosion on aluminum components is white in color. Corrosion on CRES
components is black in color.
(b) If clamps are removed, do an inspection of the tubing for signs of corrosion on the
surface where the clamp touches the tubing.
(c) If corrosion is found, remove the corrosion: SRM 51-10-02
CAUTION
DO NOT APPLY CORROSION INHIBITING COMPOUND, G00009 TO
SILICONE RUBBER, OR RUBBER CLAMP CUSHIONS. IT CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO SILICONE RUBBER.
(d) Use a cotton wiper, G00034 moist with corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 to apply a
thin layer of the compound to the hydraulic line. Application of Corrosion Inhibiting
Compound, TASK 51-21-91-620-802
29-00-00
SUBTASK 29-00-00-916-002
(2) If the hydraulic lines have been cleaned with steam or high pressure water and detergent, do
the steps that follow:
(a) Remove unwanted moisture with a cotton wiper, G00034.
(b) Use a cotton wiper, G00034 moist with corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 to apply a
thin layer of the compound to the hydraulic line. Application of Corrosion Inhibiting
Compound, TASK 51-21-91-620-802
SUBTASK 29-00-00-916-003
(3) If the hydraulic lines get a scratch or gouge during maintenance or repair work, do the step that
follows:
(a) Use a cotton wiper, G00034 moist with corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 to apply a
thin layer of the compound to the hydraulic line. Application of Corrosion Inhibiting
Compound, TASK 51-21-91-620-802
D. Improved Corrosion Protection
NOTE: The improved corrosion protection is for external threads and cavities of hydraulic actuators
and components that are open to moisture. It is provided by the use of Batco 8401 Number
1 grease plus a bead of BMS 5-45, Type II, Class B-1/2, optional Class B-2 sealant. The
Batco grease was selected because of compatibility with O-ring seal material and fair
resistance to BMS 3-11 hydraulic fluid.
SUBTASK 29-00-00-916-004
(1) For applying the corrosion protection do the steps that follow:
(a) Apply a thin layer of the grease to the faying surfaces of threads or flanges.
(b) Assemble the component and clean off unwanted grease.
(c) Clean the areas where sealant will be applied with solvent, B00148 or equivalent.
(d) Apply a bead of sealant, A00767 to the joints that were greased.
(e) Allow the sealant to cure 48 hours and make sure that it has adhered to the surfaces.

OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR WHEN THE HYDRAULIC
POWER IS SUPPLIED.
CAUTION

THE APPLICABLE FUEL TANK HAS A MINIMUM OF 1675 LBS (760 KG)
OF FUEL IN IT . IF YOU OPERATE THE EDP FOR 2 MINUTES WITHOUT

AMBIENT TEMPERATURE BEFORE YOU CONTINUE WITH THE TEST . IF
YOU CONTINUE TO OPERATE THE EDP , THE HYDRAULIC FLUID
BECOMES TOO HOT .

SUBTASK 29-21-51-020-001
(1) Remove the pressure module [1], do these steps:

(b) Disconnect the electrical connector [16] from the low pressure switch.
(c) Disconnect the electrical connector [5] from the standby rudder shutoff valve.
(d) Install the caps on the electrical connector [4], electrical connector [5], and electrical
connector [16].
(e) Disconnect the hydraulic line [8], hydraulic line [13], hydraulic line [14], and hydraulic
line [15] from the ports of the pressure module [1].
(f) Disconnect the T-fitting from the check valve [9].
(g) Remove the reducer [7], unions [12], check valve [9], and packings [6].
1) Discard the packings [6].
(h) Drain the hydraulic fluid into a 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154.
(i) Install plugs in the hydraulic line [8], hydraulic line [13], hydraulic line [14], hydraulic
line [15], and T-fitting.
(j) If it is necessary, do this task: Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane,
TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the
Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-803.
(k) Install caps on the open fittings of the pressure module [1].
(l) Remove the mounting bolts [2] and washers [3].
(m) Remove the pressure module [1].

E. Standby Hydraulic System Module Installation
SUBTASK 29-21-51-210-001
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT UNWANTED MATERIAL DOES NOT GO INTO THE
MODULE PORTS OR THE HYDRAULIC LINES DURING THE INSTALLATION.
THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT .
(1) Make sure that the unwanted material does not go into the pressure module [1], hydraulic
line [8], hydraulic line [13], hydraulic line [14], hydraulic line [15], or T-fitting.
SUBTASK 29-21-51-420-001
(2) If the packings [6], unions [12], reducer [7], and check valve [9] are not already installed on the
pressure module [1], do these steps:
(a) Apply hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B fluid, D00054, to the new packings [6],
threads of the unions [12], reducer [7], and check valve [9].
(b) Install the packings [6], unions [12], reducer [7], and check valve [9] into the pressure
module [1].
SUBTASK 29-21-51-420-002
(3) Install the pressure module [1], do these steps:
(a) Put the pressure module [1] in its mounting position.
(b) Install the bolts [2] and washers [3].
(c) Remove the plugs that were installed from the hydraulic line [8], hydraulic line [13],
hydraulic line [14], hydraulic line [15], and T-fitting.
(d) Remove any caps that installed on the pressure module fittings during the removal.
(e) Connect the hydraulic line [8], hydraulic line [13], hydraulic line [14], and hydraulic
line [15] to the ports of the pressure module [1].
1) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic line [8] and hydraulic line [15] to 140 ±7 in-lb
(16 ±1 N·m).
2) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic line [13] and hydraulic line [14] to 270 ±14 in-lb
(31 ±2 N·m).
(f) Connect the T-fitting to the check valve [9].
(g) Remove caps from the electrical connector [4], electrical connector [5], and electrical
connector [16].
(h) Connect the electrical connector [4] to the leading edge standby shutoff valve.
(i) Connect the electrical connector [16] to the low pressure switch.
(j) Connect the electrical connector [5] to the standby rudder shutoff valve.
SUBTASK 29-21-51-710-001

E. Standby Hydraulic System Pressure Module Filter Removal
SUBTASK 29-21-51-480-001
(1) Put a container below the filter bowl [24] to catch the hydraulic fluid.
SUBTASK 29-21-51-020-002
(2) Remove the filter element [23]:
(a) Remove the lockwire.
CAUTION
PULL DOWN ON THE KNURLED RING OF THE SELF-SEAL
DISCONNECT BEFORE YOU TURN IT . IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS, TOO
MUCH TORQUE WILL BE NECESSARY TO TURN THE RING. THIS WILL
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT .
(b) Disconnect the supply line for the standby hydraulic system Electric Motor-Driven Pump
(EMDP) from the standby hydraulic reservoir at the quick-disconnect.
NOTE: The quick-disconnect is at the bottom of the standby hydraulic reservoir.
(c) Remove the filter bowl [24], packing [22] and two retainers [21].
(d) Remove the filter element [23], backup ring [20] and packing [19].
(e) Look for metal contamination in the filter element [23] and in the filter bowl [24].
1) If you find metal contamination, do these steps:
a) Replace the standby EMDP , do these tasks: Standby Hydraulic System
Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Removal, TASK 29-21-21-000-801,
Standby Hydraulic System Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Installation,
TASK 29-21-21-400-801.
b) Flush the hydraulic lines from the standby EMDP to the pressure module, do

F . Standby Hydraulic System Pressure Module Filter Installation
SUBTASK 29-21-51-420-003
(1) Install the pressure filter module [11].
(a) Lightly apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the threads of the
filter bowl [24], new packing [19], new packing [22], new backup ring [20] and new
retainers [21].
NOTE: The old backup ring and retainers from the removal procedure can be used again
if you do not find damage.
(b) Install the new packing [19] and backup ring [20] in the groove on top of the filter
element [23].
(c) Install the retainers [21] and new packing [22] in the groove in the module housing.
(d) Fill the filter bowl [24] approximately half full with hydraulic fluid, D00153.
(e) Put the filter element [23] in the pressure module housing.
(f) Install the filter bowl [24] into the pressure module housing.
(g) Tighten the filter bowl [24] to 350 in-lb (39.5 N·m) - 375 in-lb (42.4 N·m).
(h) Install a MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT BEFORE
YOU INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . IF
TOO MUCH TORQUE IS NECESSARY , DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL
DISCONNECT , AND MAKE SURE THAT THE POPPET IS STRAIGHT .
AFTER YOU INSTALL IT , MAKE SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS
EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 IN. (1.52 MM). IF THE INDICATOR PINS
ARE NOT CORRECTLY EXTENDED, FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR
STOP . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE RESERVOIR, AND THE
PUMP .
(i) Connect the supply line for the standby hydraulic system Electric Motor-Driven Pump
(EMDP) to the standby hydraulic reservoir at the quick-disconnect.
NOTE: The quick-disconnect is at the bottom of the standby hydraulic reservoir.

2. Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization
(Figure 201)
A. General
(1) There are two methods for pressurizing the hydraulic reservoirs. The first method requires
pressurization of the pneumatic system's crossover manifold using the engines, Auxiliary
Power Unit (APU), or external ground air cart. The second method does not require
pressurization of the pneumatic crossover manifold, but utilizes an external air source
connected to the air charging valve manifold to pressurize the reservoirs for ground
maintenance.
29-09-00
RYR 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187,
189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; RYR
006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 POST SB 737-29-1106 (Continued)

E. Reservoir Pressurization with the Pneumatic System Pressurized (Method 1)
SUBTASK 29-09-00-480-001
WARNING
MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING
GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR COULD
RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT .
(1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing
Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-210-001
(2) Get access to the air charging valve manifold assembly in the right main landing gear wheel
well.
(a) Make sure that the air charging valve is fully closed and a dust cap is installed on the
valve stem.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-001
(3) To pressurize the pneumatic crossover manifold, do either of these tasks:
(a) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with One or Both Engines,
TASK 36-00-00-860-804.
(b) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with the APU,
TASK 36-00-00-860-803.
(c) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with an External Ground Air
Source, TASK 36-00-00-860-802.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-210-002
(4) Make note of the reservoir pressure indication on the air pressure gauge in the right main
landing gear wheel well, and the duct pressure indication on the bleed air pressure gauge in
the flight compartment (P5-10 panel).
29-09-00
RYR 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187,
189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; RYR
006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 POST SB 737-29-1106 (Continued)
SUBTASK 29-09-00-210-003
(5) Make sure that the pressure difference between the reservoir air pressure gauge and the bleed
air pressure gauge is not more than 10 psi, if the pneumatic source is the same.
NOTE: A pressure difference greater than 10 psi may be an indication of an air leak in the
reservoir pressurization system. Normal reservoir pressure should be 45-50 psi,
however, the approximate operating range can vary between 12-65 psi depending on
pneumatic source available and aircraft operation.
NOTE: If there was a different pneumatic source that pressurized the hydraulic system, the
check valves can keep the pressure in the reservoir pressurization system. Thus, the
pressure difference between the reservoir air pressure gage and the bleed air pressure
gage will be more than 10 psi.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-210-004
(6) Make sure that the reservoir air pressure indication remains stable and does not decrease.
NOTE: If the pressure decreases, there may be an air leak in the reservoir pressurization
system.
F . Reservoir Pressurization with an External Air Source (Method 2)
SUBTASK 29-09-00-480-002
WARNING
MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING
GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR COULD
RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT .
(1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing
Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-002
(2) Make sure that the pneumatic system is depressurized (engines, APU, and external air
sources are off).
SUBTASK 29-09-00-010-001
(3) Get access to the air charging valve manifold assembly in the right main landing gear wheel
well.
(a) Remove the dust cap from the valve stem on the air charging valve.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-480-003
(4) Connect the external ground regulated air source, STD-77 to the valve stem on the air
charging valve.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-980-001
(5) Turn the swivel nut on the air charging valve to the fully open position (1 to 2-1/4 turns).
29-09-00
RYR 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187,
189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; RYR
006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 POST SB 737-29-1106 (Continued)
SUBTASK 29-09-00-780-001
CAUTION
DO NOT USE MORE THAN 70 PSIG (482.633 KPA) PRESSURE. IF YOU USE
MORE THAN 70 PSIG (482.633 KPA) PRESSURE, DAMAGE TO THE
EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(6) Supply and adjust the pressure of the external ground regulated air source, STD-77 to
pressurize the reservoirs to 45-50 psi.
(a) Make sure that the reservoir air pressure gauge in the right main landing gear wheel well
shows approximately 45-50 psi.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-980-002
(7) Turn the swivel nut on the air charging valve to the fully closed position (1 to 2-1/4 turns).
(a) Make sure that the reservoir air pressure gauge indication is stable at approximately
45-50 psi.
(b) Torque the swivel nut to 50 in-lb (6 N·m) - 70 in-lb (8 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-09-00-080-001
(8) Disconnect the external ground regulated air source, STD-77 from the valve stem on the air
charging valve.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-420-001
(9) Re-install the dust cap to the valve stem on the air charging valve.

3. Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization

A. Tools/Equipment

134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-014
(1) Make sure the reservoir depressurization (vent) valve for each system reservoir is in the closed
(non-vented) position.
NOTE: The two hydraulic reservoirs are pressurized at the same time when the two reservoir
depressurization (vent) valves are closed.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-015
CAUTION
DO NOT USE MORE THAN 70 PSIG PRESSURE. IF YOU USE TOO MUCH
PRESSURE, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(2) Connect the regulated air source, STD-77 to the valve for manual air pressurization.
NOTE: The valve is on the reservoir pressurization module.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-780-002
(3) Turn the nut on the valve body to pressurize the reservoir.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-016
(4) Adjust the pressure of the regulated air source, STD-77 to pressurize the reservoir to 46 +/- 1
psig.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-017
(5) Close the valve for manual air pressurization.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-210-012
(6) Make sure the pressure in the reservoir stays stable.
NOTE: The air pressure lines between the reservoir pressurization module and the reservoirs
contain vent orifices. These orifices bleed the air pressure out of the lines after the air
source is removed. The check valves in the depressurization valves hold air pressure
in each reservoir.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-080-003
(7) Disconnect the regulated air source, STD-77 from the valve for the manual air pressurization.

(3) To pressurize the pneumatic crossover manifold, do either of these tasks:
29-09-00
RYR 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187,

006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 POST SB 737-29-1106 (Continued)
(a) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with One or Both Engines,
TASK 36-00-00-860-804.
(b) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with the APU,
TASK 36-00-00-860-803.
(c) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with an External Ground Air
Source, TASK 36-00-00-860-802.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-160-001
(4) Use a soap and water solution to check air lines and fittings for leaks after the pneumatic
system has been pressurized the first time during the leakage test.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-210-007
(5) Make note of the reservoir pressure indication on the air pressure gauge in the right main
landing gear wheel well, and the duct pressure indication on the bleed air pressure gauge in
the flight compartment (P5-10 panel).
SUBTASK 29-09-00-210-008
(6) Make sure the pressure difference between the reservoir air pressure gauge and the bleed air
pressure gauge is not more than 10 psi.
NOTE: A pressure difference greater than 10 psi may be an indication of an air leak in the
reservoir pressurization system. Normal reservoir pressure should be 45-50 psi,
however, the approximate operating range canl vary between 12-65 psi depending on
pneumatic source available and aircraft operation.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-210-009
(7) Make sure the reservoir air pressure indication remains stable and does not decrease.
NOTE: If the pressure decreases, there may be an air leak in the reservoir pressurization
system.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-007
(8) Do this task: Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-210-010
(9) Make sure the reservoir air pressure indication remains stable and does not decrease for at
least 15 minutes.
NOTE: If the pressure decreases, there may be an air leak in the reservoir pressurization
system or contamination in the restrictor/check valve crosses.
(a) If the air pressure indication does not remain stable, then make sure the check valves in
the cross-fitting assemblies are not contaminated.
1) If contamination is found in the check valves in the cross-fitting assemblies, flush
with alcohol, B00130.
2) Wipe clean and dry with a lint free cloth.
(b) Use a solution of soap and water to check that there are no air leaks at the pressurization
tube connections between the air pressure filter assembly near the pneumatic crossover
manifold duct in the left/right ECS bays and the air charging valve manifold assembly in
the right main landing gear wheel well.
29-09-00

(P/B 401)

Reference Description
STD-1115 Source - Nitrogen, 0-100 PSIG

Reference Description Specification
G00091 Compound - Oxygen System Leak Detection -
Snoop Leak Detector
MIL-PRF-25567
D. Location Zones
Zone Area
133 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Left
134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right
E. Procedure
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-021
(1) Make sure the two engines and the APU are off.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-420-003
(2) Attach the DO-NOT-USE tag to the pneumatic ground service connector.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-022
(3) Release the pressure from the hydraulic reservoirs. To release it, do this task: Hydraulic
Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-023
(4) Make sure the reservoirs for the hydraulic systems A and B are filled with hydraulic fluid. To fill
them, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801.
29-09-00
RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 PRE SB 737-29-1106 (Continued)
SUBTASK 29-09-00-210-013
(5) Do a check of the vent caps for the pneumatic supply lines:
(a) Remove the vent caps from the pneumatic supply lines from the right and left pneumatic
ducts.
NOTE: One vent cap is installed at approximately RBL 25 on the forward bulkhead. The
other vent cap is installed at approximately LBL 30 on the forward bulkhead.
(b) Make sure the vents are free of corrosion and material that can cause blockage.
(c) If there is corrosion and blockage, then replace them with new vent caps.
(d) Install the vent caps.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-020-002
(6) Disconnect the pneumatic supply lines from the hydraulic reservoir pressurization module.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-420-004
(7) Install plugs on pneumatic supply lines.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-210-014
(8) Do a check of the vent cap assembly for the hydraulic reservoir pressurization module:
(a) Remove the vent cap assembly from the orifice assembly.
(b) Make sure the vent cap assembly is free of corrosion and material that can cause
blockage.
(c) If there is corrosion and blockage, then replace it with a new vent cap assembly.
NOTE: Do not install the new vent cap assembly until you complete this task.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-080-005
(9) Install the BACC14AD04D cap in the location of the vent cap assembly for the orifice
assembly.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-080-006
(10) Connect a nitrogen 0-100 PSIG nitrogen source, STD-1115 to the valve for the manual air
pressurization.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-024
(11) Do these steps to slowly pressurize the reservoirs:
(a) Turn the nut on the valve for the manual air pressurization.
CAUTION
DO NOT USE MORE THAN 70 PSIG PRESSURE. IF YOU USE TOO
MUCH PRESSURE, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(b) Adjust the pressure regulator for the nitrogen 0-100 PSIG nitrogen source, STD-1115 until
the relief valves for the hydraulic reservoirs open.
(c) Make sure the two relief valves open at 60 to 65 psi.
(d) Reduce pressure to 50 psig.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-790-001
(12) Do these steps to check for air leakage at the ports for the pneumatic supply lines:
NOTE: For pressurization modules that have a filter drain vent, block it.
29-09-00
RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 PRE SB 737-29-1106 (Continued)
(a) Apply Snoop Leak Detector compound, G00091 to the ports for the pneumatic supply
lines on the hydraulic reservoir pressurization module.
(b) Make sure there is no air leakage at the ports for the pneumatic supply lines.
NOTE: If there is air leakage, the Snoop Leak Detector compound, G00091 will have
bubbles.
(c) If there is air leakage at the ports for the pneumatic supply lines, then do these checks:
NOTE: On pressurization modules with the filter drain vent, make sure the vent is no
longer restricted.
1) If there is air leakage at one or both of the ports, then replace the applicable check
valve or check valves.
2) If necessary, replace the Hydraulic Reservoir Pressurization Module.
These are the tasks:
• Hydraulic Reservoir Pressurization Module - Removal, TASK 29-09-06-000-805,
• Hydraulic Reservoir Pressurization Module - Installation, TASK 29-09-06-400-805.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-025
(13) Make sure that the reservoir pressure is greater than 50 psi.
(a) If the reservoir pressure is less than 50 psi, supply pressure with nitrogen 0-100 PSIG
nitrogen source, STD-1115.
(b) Close the shutoff valve for the 0-100 PSIG nitrogen source, STD-1115.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-790-002
(14) Do a leakage check of the lines with gauge, STD-1292 for the hydraulic reservoirs A and B
(Figure 501, Figure 502):
(a) Make sure the gage pressure does not decrease more than 5 psi in five minutes.
(b) If the gage pressure decreases more than 5 psi in five minutes, then do these steps:
1) Pressurize the hydraulic reservoir to 50 psi with 0-100 PSIG nitrogen source,
STD-1115.
2) Apply Snoop Leak Detector compound, G00091 to all fittings and valves on the
hydraulic reservoir, and all lines back to the hydraulic reservoir pressurization
module.
3) Make sure that there is no leakage at all the fitting and valves on the hydraulic
reservoir, and all the lines back to the hydraulic reservoir pressurization module.
NOTE: If there is leakage, the Snoop Leak Detector compound, G00091 will have
bubbles.
4) If there is leakage, tighten the fittings or replace the applicable component that
causes the leakage.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-026
(15) Depressurize the reservoirs. To depressurize them, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs
Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-020-003
(16) Remove the BACC14AD04D cap from the orifice assembly.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-420-005
(17) Install a clean vent cap assembly on to the orifice assembly.
29-09-00
RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 PRE SB 737-29-1106 (Continued)
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-027
CAUTION
DO NOT USE MORE THAN 70 PSIG PRESSURE. IF YOU USE TOO MUCH
PRESSURE, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(18) Adjust the pressure regulator for the 0-100 PSIG nitrogen source, STD-1115 until the reservoir
pressure is 50 psi.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-028
(19) Close the shutoff valve for the 0-100 PSIG nitrogen source, STD-1115.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-790-003
(20) If the gage pressure decreases more than 5 psi in 5 minutes, then do this step (Figure 501,
Figure 502):
(a) Replace the check valve in the tee valve assembly.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-080-007
(21) Remove the nitrogen 0-100 PSIG nitrogen source, STD-1115.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-029
(22) Depressurize the reservoirs. To depressurize them, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs
Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-020-004
(23) Remove plugs on pneumatic supply lines.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-420-006
(24) Connect the pneumatic supply lines to the hydraulic reservoir pressurization module.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-860-030
(25) Pressurize the hydraulic system A and B reservoirs. To pressurize them, do this task: Hydraulic
Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-807.
SUBTASK 29-09-00-420-007
(26) Make sure there is no leakage of air at the connections to the reservoir pressurization module.

F . Secondary Check Valve Installation
SUBTASK 29-09-01-020-010
(1) Remove any plugs/caps from the tube ends, air pressure filter assembly [1], and check
valve [8].
RYR 068-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-156 PRE SB 737-29-1106;
AIRPLANES WITH FILTER ASSEMBLY PART NUMBER 7595270-103
SUBTASK 29-09-01-420-009
(2) Do these steps to install the secondary check valve [8] in the air pressure filter assembly [1]:
(a) Put a thin coating of primer, C50500, on the face of the check valve hex that will contact
the filter head.
(b) Put a thin coating of grease, D50099, on the threads of the check valve [8].
(c) Put the check valve [8] in the outlet port of the air pressure filter assembly [1].
(d) Tighten the check valve [8] to 162 in-lb (18.3 N·m) - 178 in-lb (20.1 N·m).
RYR 157-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304,

WITH FILTER ASSEMBLY PART NUMBER 1732030-01

G. Post-Installation Leakage Check
SUBTASK 29-09-01-860-010
(1) Pressurize the hydraulic reservoir using method 1 (pneumatic system pressurized)
(TASK 29-09-00-860-801).
SUBTASK 29-09-01-790-002
(2) Use a solution of soap and water to check for air leakage at the swivel nut connection on the
check valve and at the check valve connection on the filter assembly.
(a) If air leakage is found, clean and retighten the check valve connections.
SUBTASK 29-09-01-860-011
(3) Depressurize the pneumatic system (TASK 36-00-00-860-806).
SUBTASK 29-09-01-860-012

WARNING

assembly to become cool before you touch it.
F . Manifold Assembly Removal
SUBTASK 29-09-02-860-004
(1) Make sure that the hydraulic reservoirs are depressurized before you remove the manifold
assembly [1] (TASK 29-09-00-860-802).
SUBTASK 29-09-02-020-001
(2) Loosen the tube assembly nuts [5] to disconnect the tube assemblies from the elbow [12] and
union [6] on the manifold assembly [1].
SUBTASK 29-09-02-020-002
(3) Remove the bolts [2] and washers [3] that attach the manifold assembly [1] to the bracket.
SUBTASK 29-09-02-020-007
(4) Remove the manifold assembly [1].
SUBTASK 29-09-02-020-008
(5) Remove the elbow [12] from the union [6].
SUBTASK 29-09-02-020-003
(6) Remove the unions [6] from the manifold assembly [1].
(a) Remove and discard the packings [7] (o-rings) from the unions [6].
(b) Set aside unions [6] for later installation.
SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-001
(7) Install cap/plug, STD-14686, to the tube assembly nuts [5] and ports of manifold assembly [1].
G. Air Charging Valve Removal
SUBTASK 29-09-02-860-005
(1) Make sure that the hydraulic reservoirs are depressurized before you remove the charging
valve [4] (TASK 29-09-00-860-802).
SUBTASK 29-09-02-020-004
(2) Remove the lockwire from the charging valve [4] and manifold assembly [1]
(TASK 20-10-44-000-801).
SUBTASK 29-09-02-020-005
(3) Remove the charging valve [4] from the manifold assembly [1].
(a) Remove and discard the packing [11] (o-ring) from the charging valve [4].

SUBTASK 29-09-02-020-006
(1) Remove the cap/plug, STD-14686, from the tube assembly nuts [5] and ports of manifold
assembly [1].
SUBTASK 29-09-02-640-001
(2) Lightly lubricate the new packings [7] (O-rings) with MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid,
D00153.
SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-008
(3) Install the new packings [7] (O-rings) onto the unions [6].
SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-002
(4) Install the unions [6] into the ports of manifold assembly [1] and tighten to 150 in-lb (17 N·m) -
300 in-lb (34 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-010
(5) Install the elbow [12] onto the union [6] and tighten to 133 in-lb (15 N·m) - 147 in-lb (17 N·m).

SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-004

(15 N·m) - 147 in-lb (17 N·m).
29-09-02
F . Air Charging Valve Installation
SUBTASK 29-09-02-640-002
(1) Lightly lubricate the new packing [11] (O-ring) with MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid,
D00153.
SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-009
(2) Install the packing [11] (O-ring) onto the charging valve [4].
SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-005
NOTE: Clean top surface of BOSS and insure that it is free from nicks and scratches before
installing charging valve.
(3) Insert the charging valve [4] into the port of the manifold assembly [1].
(a) Tighten the charging valve [4] to 100 in-lb (11 N·m) - 110 in-lb (12 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-006
(4) Install a MS20995C47 lockwire, G50356, to the air charging valve [4] and manifold
assembly [1] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
SUBTASK 29-09-02-420-007
(5) Make sure that the dust cap [9] is installed to extreme finger tightness and the swivel nut [8] is
turned to the fully closed position on the charging valve [4].
(a) Tighten the swivel nut [8] to 50 in-lb (6 N·m) - 70 in-lb (8 N·m).

manifold assembly [1] and charging valve [4].
SUBTASK 29-09-02-860-008
(3) If it is necessary, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802.

(1) Do this task: Hydraulic Power System - Activation, TASK 29-00-00-800-802.

E. Pressure Relief Valve Installation
SUBTASK 29-09-05-020-005
(1) Remove the plugs/caps from the tube ends and pressure relief valve ports.
SUBTASK 29-09-05-640-001
(2) Lightly lubricate the new packings [3] (o-rings) with MCS 352B fluid, D00054 or hydraulic fluid,
D00153.
SUBTASK 29-09-05-420-002
(3) Install the packings [3] (o-rings) and the unions [2] to the pressure relief valve ports, and
tighten.
SUBTASK 29-09-05-420-003
(4) Install the pressure relief valve [1] and tighten the swivel nuts.
NOTE: The 'IN-OUT' flow arrow on the pressure relief valve [1] must point away from the
adjacent cross fitting assembly. The inlet side of the pressure relief valve [1] is
adjacent to the cross fitting assembly. The outlet side of the pressure relief valve [1] is
adjacent to the APU fuel line shroud drain mast tubing.
SUBTASK 29-09-05-420-004
(5) Install the clamp [6], washers [5], and screws [4] to the pressure relief valve [1].
F . Post-Installation Leakage Check
SUBTASK 29-09-05-860-005
(1) Pressurize the pneumatic crossover manifold duct.
SUBTASK 29-09-05-790-001
(2) Use a solution of soap and water to check that no air leaks at the swivel nut connection on the
inlet side of the pressure relief valve [1].
SUBTASK 29-09-05-860-006
(3) Depressurize the pneumatic cross manifold duct.
SUBTASK 29-09-05-860-007
(4) If necessary, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802

A. References
Reference Title

36-00-00-860-806 Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System (P/B 201)
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right
C. Prepare for the Removal
SUBTASK 29-09-06-860-026
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU REMOVE PRESSURE FROM THE PNEUMATIC
MANIFOLD. IF YOU DO NOT REMOVE PRESSURE, INJURY TO PERSONS
AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(1) Set the ENG 1, ENG 2, and APU BLEED switches, on the forward overhead panel P5, to the
OFF position (TASK 36-00-00-860-806).
SUBTASK 29-09-06-860-027
(2) Attach the DO-NOT-USE tag to the pneumatic ground service connector.
SUBTASK 29-09-06-860-028
(3) Release the pressure from the hydraulic reservoirs. To release it, do this task: Hydraulic
Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808.
D. Pressurization Module Removal
SUBTASK 29-09-06-020-013
(1) Disconnect the hydraulic tube [1] from the orifice assembly [13].
SUBTASK 29-09-06-020-014
(2) Disconnect the pneumatic supply lines [10] from the pressurization module [2].
29-09-06
SUBTASK 29-09-06-020-015
(3) Install caps on the pneumatic supply lines [10] and the tube [1] and the ports in the
pressurization module [2].
SUBTASK 29-09-06-020-016
(4) Remove the pressurization module [2]:
(a) Remove the bolts [3] and washers [4] from the pressurization module [2].
(b) Remove the pressurization module [2] from the airplane.
SUBTASK 29-09-06-020-017
(5) Remove these parts from the pressurization module [2] if they are necessary for the
replacement pressurization module [2]:
(a) Remove the orifice assembly [13] from the pressurization module [2].
1) Remove the nut [14], retainer [18], packing [17], backup ring [16], and packing [15].
2) Make a record of position of the packing [17], backup ring [16], and packing [15].
3) Discard the backup ring [16] and packings [15] [17].
(b) Remove the plug [7] and packing [11] from the test port [12].
1) Discard the packing [11].
(c) Remove the reducers [9] and packings [7] from the pneumatic supply ports.
1) Discard the packings [7].

C. Procedure
SUBTASK 29-09-06-640-004
(1) Install these parts in the new pressurization module [2] if they are not installed:
(a) The orifice assembly [13]:
1) Lubricate the threads, packing [17], packing [15], and backup ring [16] with MCS
352B fluid, D00054 or hydraulic fluid, D00153.
2) Install the nut [14], retainer [18], packing [17], backup ring [16], and packing [15] on
the orifice assembly [13].
3) Install the orifice assembly [13] on the pressurization module [2] but do not tighten
it.
(b) The plug [7] in the test port [12]:
1) Lubricate the packing [11] with MCS 352B fluid, D00054 or hydraulic fluid, D00153.
2) Install the packing [11] on the plug [7].
3) Install the plug [7] on the pressurization module [2].
4) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912.
(c) The reducers [9] in the pneumatic supply ports:
1) Lubricate the packing [8] with MCS 352B fluid, D00054 or hydraulic fluid, D00153.
2) Lubricate the threads of the reducers [9] with primer, C00259.
3) Install the packing [8] on the reducers [9].
4) Install the reducers [9] in the pressurization module [2].
SUBTASK 29-09-06-420-015
(2) Install the pressurization module [2]:
(a) Put the pressurizationmodule [2] in its position.
(b) Install the bolts [3] and washers [4] to attach the pressurizationmodule [2] to the bracket.
29-09-06
SUBTASK 29-09-06-420-016
(3) Remove the caps from the hydraulic tube [1] and the pneumatic supply lines [10].
SUBTASK 29-09-06-420-017
(4) Connect the hydraulic tube [1] to the orifice assembly [13]:
(a) Adjust the orifice assembly [13] until you can connect the hydraulic tube [1].
(b) Tighten the orifice assembly [13].
SUBTASK 29-09-06-420-018
(5) Connect the pneumatic supply lines [10] to the pressurization module [2].

(1) Remove the DO-NOT-USE tag from the connector for the ground pneumatic air.
SUBTASK 29-09-06-790-008

TASK 29-09-06-790-803.

7. Hydraulic System A or B Flushing
A. General
(1) This procedure flushes the hydraulic system after you replace a hydraulic pump because of a
mechanical malfunction, or if you find metal contamination in the filter.
(2) If the airplane experiences repeated failures of a pump at one location, there may be debris in
the case drain line, case drain hose, case drain hose quick-disconnect or case drain filter
module check valve contamination that cannot be flushed by accomplishing this procedure.
Careful examination, cleaning, or replacement of the case drain hose or quick-disconnect may
be required.
29-11-00
(3) If contamination from a damaged pump is found when you flush the hydraulic system, then it is
recommended to do these steps:
NOTE: Operator experience shows that a new filter can become plugged by debris that
remains in the hydraulic system after a mechanical failure. A plugged filter can cause
hydraulic fluid to bypass the filter element and allow debris to circulate in the system.
Debris that bypasses the filter can cause a premature failure of a new hydraulic pump.
(a) Examine the case drain line and hoses for contamination or blockage.
(b) If contamination or blockage is found, clean or replace the case drain line.
(c) Replace the case drain filter element again, at the next maintenance opportunity following
one week of normal operation.
(d) Replace all the filter elements in the system at the next maintenance opportunity
following two months of normal operation.
(4) If the contamination of the hydraulic fluid is from a chemical source, replace the fluid and the
filter elements.

BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU CUT THE LOCK WIRE FROM THE FILTER
ASSEMBLY . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SURFACE OF THE
BARREL AND HEAD ASSEMBLY .
(a) Remove and discard lockwires from the acoustic filter assembly [4].
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU CAREFULLY DRAIN HYDRAULIC FLUID INTO A
SUITABLE CONTAINER. CAREFULLY CLEAN, DRY , AND DISPOSE OF
ALL LEAKAGE. HYDRAULIC FLUID CAUSES DAMAGE TO RUBBER,
COPPER, PLASTICS, PAINTS, AND MANY OTHER MATERIALS.
(b) Use the wrenching flats on the barrel and head to disassemble the acoustic filter
assembly [4].
(c) Remove and discard the packing [1], packing [2], and backup rings [3].
(d) Use solvent, B00184, or equivalent to flush all surfaces and let air dry.
(e) Examine all surfaces, packing grooves, and threads for defects or contamination.
(f) Install the new packing [1], new packing [2], and new backup rings [3]
(TASK 20-10-31-400-801).
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU CORRECTLY ALIGN AND INSTALL BACKUP
RINGS. EXTRUSION AND LEAKS CAN OCCUR IF YOU DO NOT
CORRECTLY INSTALL BACKUP RINGS.
1) Make sure that the spiral-cut teflon backup rings [3] are aligned and installed
correctly.
(g) Apply hydraulic fluid, D50122, to the threads of the filter head and filter barrel.
(h) Assemble the acoustic filter assembly [4].

(i) Tighten the filter head to 480 in-lb (54 N·m) - 540 in-lb (61 N·m).
1) Use the wrenching flats on the filter barrel and filter head.

F . Repair Procedures for Damage on the Flow Tube
SUBTASK 29-11-00-200-003
(1) If the flow tube is damaged or corroded discard the unit or return to manufacturer for
evaluation and or replacement.
NOTE: Do not attempt to repair.
(2) If the flow tube is not damaged, then make sure that the three long holes (flow passages) are
clean and clear of foreign objects.
(3) To clean the flow tube do this task: Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump
(EMDP) Acoustic Filter Cleaning, TASK 29-11-00-100-801.
G. Repair Procedures for Damage on the Barrel
SUBTASK 29-11-00-200-004
CAUTION
DO NOT REPAIR MORE THAN 5 PERCENT ON THE MATERIAL, IF THE
REPAIR IS MORE THAN 5 PERCENT , REPLACE THE ASSEMBLY .
NOTE: Make sure that the acoustic filter components are protected at all time of procedure.
(1) If the damage or corrosion on the barrel exceeds the damage limit of 0.010 in. (0.254 mm) or is
within the NO REWORK area, discard the unit or return to manufacturer for evaluation and or
replacement.
NOTE: Do not attempt to repair.
(2) For scratches, dents, blistering, flaking, corrosion, and pitting that will require removal of less
then 0.010 in. (0.254 mm) of material, do these steps:
(a) Cover all openings to avoid contamination.
(b) Remove damage by lightly sanding or with a lathe.
NOTE: Use abrasive paper, G50339, or emery cloth, G00744 to remove damage.
(c) Do a Liquid Penetrant, G51208 test to make sure that there are no cracks on the barrel.
(d) Clean the repair and apply a protective film with Bonderite M-CR 1132 Aero coating,
C50079 or coating, C00851 to the repair.
H. Repair Procedure for Damage on the Head
SUBTASK 29-11-00-200-005
(1) If the damage or corrosion on the head exceeds the damage limit of 0.004 in. (0.102 mm) or is
within the NO REWORK area, discard the unit or return to manufacturer for evaluation and or
replacement.
NOTE: Do not attempt to repair.
(2) For scratches, dents, blistering, flaking, corrosion, and pitting that will require removal of less
then 0.004 in. (0.102 mm) of material, do these steps:
(a) Cover all openings to avoid contamination.
(b) Remove damage by lightly sanding.
NOTE: Use abrasive paper, G50339, or emery cloth, G00744 to remove damage.
(c) Do a Liquid Penetrant, G51208 test to make sure that there are no cracks on the head.
(d) Clean the repair and apply a protective film with Bonderite M-CR 1132 Aero coating,
C50079 or coating, C00851 to the repair.
29-11-00

between 2800 psig (19,305 kPa) and 3200 psig (22,063 kPa).

2. Hydraulic Fluid - Check
(Figure 601)
A. General
(1) You must supply clean bottles which will hold the fluid samples. If you do not do this, it is
possible that the fluid samples will not be correct.
(2) Supply clean sample bottles from a satisfactory laboratory, or a vendor (for example, Fisher,
Catalog #02-893-5D or equivalent). Use non-powdered gloves to prevent contamination during
the sampling procedure. Remove the bottle cap immediately before you collect the sample. Put
the cap face down on a clean (lint-free, dirt-free) surface during sampling.
(a) If the first sample has a high particle count, you can sample the hydraulic fluid again with
the hydraulic fluid check task.
NOTE: This will show, if there was contamination during the sampling procedure and
could prevent replacing all the systems fluid.
(3) You must get one hydraulic fluid sample from each hydraulic reservoir.
(4) A polyethylene bottle (500ml), STD-1104, or a capacity 2 ounces, with polyethylene screw cap
and seal, glass bottle, STD-1105, can be used to collect the hydraulic fluid.
NOTE: The glass bottle is shown as an alternate choice because low quality polyethylene
containers can allow organic contaminants to pass into the oil sample and affect the
test results. Polyethylene containers made from high grade PE, especially those
obtained from the hydraulic fluid supplier, are permitted for use.

SUBTASK 29-11-00-160-001
(1) Clean the drain valve on the reservoir with cotton wiper, G00034.
(a) Make sure that there is no contamination in the port before you drain the fluid.
SUBTASK 29-11-00-680-008

WARNING

WATER. IF YOU GET HYDRAULIC FLUID IN YOUR EYES, FLUSH YOUR
EYES WITH WATER AND GET MEDICAL AID. IF YOU EAT OR DRINK THE
HYDRAULIC FLUID, GET MEDICAL AID.
(3) Open the reservoir drain valve to supply a smooth flow of fluid into the 5 gallon (19 liter)
container, STD-1154.
SUBTASK 29-11-00-680-002

hydraulic system reservoir gets fluid from the hydraulic system B.
(a) Put the bottle in the fluid flow but do not touch the reservoir drain valve.
(b) When the bottle is full, remove it from the fluid flow.
NOTE: Do not close the reservoir drain valve, while the bottle is in the fluid flow. This will
prevent contamination of the sample.

(a) Airplane model
(b) Airplane number
(c) Hydraulic system number
(d) Date
(e) Location.

required (TASK 29-00-00-900-801).

H. Heat Exchanger Installation
SUBTASK 29-11-04-650-003
WARNING
OBEY THE PRECAUTIONS FOR PURGING AND FUEL TANK ENTRY . IF YOU
DO NOT OBEY THE PRECAUTIONS, INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(1) Prepare the fuel tank before you go into it (TASK 28-11-00-910-802).
SUBTASK 29-11-04-420-001
(2) Put the heat exchanger [1] through the main tank access door.
NOTE: Put the end of the heat exchanger [1] with the inlet port [11] and outlet port [13] in first.
SUBTASK 29-11-04-420-002
(3) T emporarily install washer [6], washer [4], washer [3], bolt [2], and nut [5].
SUBTASK 29-11-04-420-003
(4) T emporarily install washer [6], washer [15], bonding jumper [14], washer [3], bolt [16],
washer [4], and nut [5].
SUBTASK 29-11-04-420-004
(5) If it is necessary, install an additional washer [15] to provide clearance between the bonding
jumper [14] and heat exchanger [1].
SUBTASK 29-11-04-420-006
(6) Measure the clearance between the washer [6] and the heat exchanger [1].
(a) If the clearance is more than 0.007 in. (0.178 mm), add additional washer [6] to fill the
clearance.
SUBTASK 29-11-04-420-007
(7) Tighten the nuts [5].
SUBTASK 29-11-04-420-008
(8) Install the washers [8], washers [9], bolts [7], and nuts [10].
SUBTASK 29-11-04-420-009
(9) Connect the inlet port [11] and the outlet port [13] of the new heat exchanger to the hydraulic
lines by performing one of the following methods, shown in Figure 404 and Figure 405 (based
on which action was taken during heat exchanger removal).
(a) Method (a) hydraulic tubes to new heat exchanger replaced with new tubes (Figure 405
and Figure 407).
29-11-04
1) Install new tube runs of the same part number with new externally swaged fittings
(TASK 20-10-51-400-808).
a) Obey the requirements for bonding and grounding/faying surfaces on
permaswage bulkhead penetration fittings during part installation
(TASK 29-11-55-400-801).
b) Keep sufficient tube clearances (TASK 20-10-51-200-801).
c) Use the kept support clamps and fasteners.
CAUTION
USE TWO WRENCHES TO DISCONNECT OR CONNECT TUBES. IF
YOU DO NOT USE A WRENCH ON EACH SIDE OF THE
CONNECTION, DAMAGE TO THE TUBES CAN OCCUR.
2) Connect the hydraulic lines to the penetration fittings (TASK 29-11-55-400-801).
(b) Method (b) new heat exchanger spliced to existing hydraulic heat exchanger tubes
(Figure 406 and Figure 408).
1) Cut replacement sections (tube splices) from new tubes of the correct part numbers
or make tube splices from 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) diameter and 0.035 in. (0.889 mm) wall
thickness, 6061-T6 aluminum tubing (AMS4083).
a) Use removed (kept) tube sections as the pattern.
b) Use the replacement tubes to connect the new heat exchanger to the
remaining tube sections (TASK 20-10-51-300-805).
NOTE: There is one recommended location for the heat exchanger (hydraulic
system A) in the left wing and two optional locations (for inlet port [11]
and outlet port [13]) for the heat exchanger (hydraulic system B) in the
right wing.
2) Install the tube splices (TASK 20-10-51-400-808).
a) Obey the electrical resistance requirements for permaswage fittings during
part installation/swaging (TASK 20-10-51-760-801).
b) Keep sufficient tube clearances (TASK 20-10-51-200-801).
c) Use the kept support clamps and fasteners.
SUBTASK 29-11-04-410-004
(10) Install the fuel tubes before the heat exchanger removal and replacement
(TASK 28-22-15-400-801).
(a) Obey the electrical bonding requirements.
SUBTASK 29-11-04-940-001
(11) Make sure that you remove all of the tools, unwanted parts, and unwanted objects from the
wing fuel tank.

28-AWL-10: CDCCL
SUBTASK 29-11-04-210-001
(1) Make sure that the bonding jumper [14] is installed from the heat exchanger [1] to the structure
inside the tank.

for important information on Critical Design Configuration Control Limitations
(CDCCLs).
NOTE: This is applicable to Airworthiness Limitation 28-AWL-10.
SUBTASK 29-11-04-860-011
28-AWL-10: CDCCL
(2) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the structure and the heat exchanger [1]
(SWPM 20-20-00).
NOTE: CDCCL - Refer to the Airworthiness Limitation Precautions, TASK 29-00-00-910-801,
for important information on Critical Design Configuration Control Limitations
(CDCCLs).
NOTE: This is applicable to Airworthiness Limitation 28-AWL-10.
(a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
28-AWL-10: CDCCL
(b) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.0050 ohm (5.0 milliohms) or less.
NOTE: CDCCL - Refer to the Airworthiness Limitation Precautions,
TASK 29-00-00-910-801, for important information on Critical Design
Configuration Control Limitations (CDCCLs).
NOTE: This is applicable to Airworthiness Limitation 28-AWL-10.
SUBTASK 29-11-04-760-003
28-AWL-10: CDCCL
(3) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the hydraulic heat exchanger and each
externally swaged hydraulic tube fitting (SWPM 20-20-00).
NOTE: CDCCL - Refer to the Airworthiness Limitation Precautions, TASK 29-00-00-910-801,
for important information on Critical Design Configuration Control Limitations
(CDCCLs).
NOTE: This is applicable to Airworthiness Limitation 28-AWL-10.
(a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
28-AWL-10: CDCCL
(b) Make sure the electrical bonding resistance is 0.00041 ohm (0.41 milliohm) or less.
NOTE: CDCCL - Refer to the Airworthiness Limitation Precautions,
TASK 29-00-00-910-801, for important information on Critical Design
Configuration Control Limitations (CDCCLs).
NOTE: This is applicable to Airworthiness Limitation 28-AWL-10.

SUBTASK 29-11-04-760-002
28-AWL-10: CDCCL
(4) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the hydraulic tubes and the externally
swaged hydraulic tube fittings (SWPM 20-20-00).
NOTE: CDCCL - Refer to the Airworthiness Limitation Precautions, TASK 29-00-00-910-801,
for important information on Critical Design Configuration Control Limitations
(CDCCLs).
NOTE: This is applicable to Airworthiness Limitation 28-AWL-10.
(a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.

NOTE: CDCCL - Refer to the Airworthiness Limitation Precautions,
TASK 29-00-00-910-801, for important information on Critical Design
Configuration Control Limitations (CDCCLs).
NOTE: This is applicable to Airworthiness Limitation 28-AWL-10.
NOTE: The externally swaged fittings connecting the hydraulic tubes to the heat
exchanger are reducer unions. The heat exchanger side is a 0.625 in. (15.9 mm)
and the hydraulic tube side is a 0.50 in. (12.7 mm).
SUBTASK 29-11-04-211-001
(5) Do a check of the seals on the bulkhead fittings.
(a) If it is necessary, replace the fillet seal on the bulkhead fittings on the outside of the tank.
1) Use sealant, A02315, to apply the fillet seal.
(b) If it is necessary, replace the full bodied fillet seal on the inside of the tank.
1) Use sealant, A00436, to apply a fillet seal.

WARNING
WHEN YOU OPEN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS, MAKE SURE THAT THE
OUTER DOOR STAYS AS OPEN AS POSSIBLE. IF THE OUTER DOOR
TURNS IN, THE ATTACHED DOOR COMPONENTS COULD TOUCH THE
INNER DOOR COMPONENTS. THIS CAN CAUSE AN ARC CONDITION
WHEN YOU SUPPLY POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTORS IN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS. BE
CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE
INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS POSSIBLE,
REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST . THE P91 AND P92
PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE
AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES.

SUBTASK 29-11-04-860-008
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL
CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER.
AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, LANDING
GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU
SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT .
CAUTION
DO NOT OPERATE THE EMDP FOR MORE THAN 2 MINUTES UNLESS THE
APPLICABLE FUEL TANK HAS A MINIMUM OF 1675 LBS (760 KG) OF FUEL
IN IT . IF YOU OPERATE THE EMDP FOR 2 MINUTES WITHOUT FUEL IN THE
TANK, LET THE RESERVOIR GO BACK TO AMBIENT TEMPERATURE
BEFORE YOU CONTINUE WITH THE TEST . IF YOU CONTINUE TO OPERATE
THE EMDP , THE HYDRAULIC FLUID CAN BECOME TOO HOT .

F . Ground Service Disconnect Filter Installation
SUBTASK 29-11-08-400-001
(1) Make sure that the filter fitting [2] in the module is tight, if it is not tight, do these steps:
(a) Remove the filter fitting [2].
(b) Discard the packing [3].
(c) Lubricate a new packing [3] with hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B fluid, D00054.
(d) Install the packing [3].
(e) Install the filter fitting [2] in the module and tighten it to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 200 in-lb
(22.6 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-11-08-400-002
(2) Lubricate a new packing [4] and the backup ring [5] with hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B
fluid, D00054.
29-11-08
SUBTASK 29-11-08-400-003
(3) Install the packing [4] and backup ring [5] on the filter element [6].
(a) Put the backup ring [5] below the packing [4].
SUBTASK 29-11-08-400-004
(4) Lubricate a new packing [8] and the backup rings [7] with hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS
352B fluid, D00054.
SUBTASK 29-11-08-400-005
(5) Install the packing [8] and backup rings [7] in the module.
SUBTASK 29-11-08-420-011
CAUTION
PUT HYDRAULIC FLUID IN THE FILTER BOWL BEFORE YOU INSTALL THE
FILTER BOWL. AIR CAUGHT BELOW THE FILTER ELEMENT CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO THE FILTER ELEMENT .
(6) Fill the filter bowl [9] approximately 1/3 full with hydraulic fluid, D00153.
SUBTASK 29-11-08-400-006
(7) Put the filter element [6] in the filter bowl [9].
SUBTASK 29-11-08-400-007
(8) Install the filter bowl [9] on the filter module.
(a) Tighten the filter bowl [9] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 75 in-lb (8.5 N·m) and install lockwire.
