2. Hydraulic systems A and B Engine-Driven Pump (EDP) Depressurization Solenoid Valve -
Operational Check
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) Each engine has one engine-driven pump located on the forward side of the Accessory Gear
Box (AGB) at the 3 o'clock position.
(2) The Engine 1 and Engine 2 engine-driven pumps are the same.
(3) The hydraulic hose connections have self-sealing disconnects to prevent leakage of hydraulic
fluid and to keep air out of the hydraulic system.
(4) For this procedure, the hydraulic systems A and B engine-driven pump will be referred to as
the hydraulic pump.
B. References
Reference Title
12-12-00-610-801 Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing (P/B 301)
29-09-00-860-801 Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization (P/B 201)
29-09-00-860-807 Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization (P/B 201)
29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201)
71-00-00-700-810-F00 Test 2 - Dry Motor Leak Test (P/B 501)
71-00-00-700-819-F00 Stop the Engine Procedure (Usual Engine Stop) (P/B 201)
71-00-00-700-821-F00 Dry Motor the Engine (P/B 201)
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
410 Subzone - Engine 1
420 Subzone - Engine 2
D. Depressurization Solenoid Valve Operational Check
SUBTASK 29-11-11-860-037
(1) Do this task: Test 2 - Dry Motor Leak Test, TASK 71-00-00-700-810-F00.
SUBTASK 29-11-11-860-038
(2) For engine1, make sure that the safety tag is removed and this circuit breaker is closed:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
B 15 C00779 HYD SYS ENG PUMP DEPRESS VALVE 1
29-11-11
SUBTASK 29-11-11-860-039
(3) For engine2, make sure that the safety tag is removed and this circuit breaker is closed:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
A 17 C00780 HYD SYS ENG PUMP DEPRESS VALVE 2
SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-043
(4) Pressurize the applicable hydraulic reservoir (TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or
TASK 29-09-00-860-807).
SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-044
(5) Make sure that all hydraulic pumps are not operating.
SUBTASK 29-11-11-860-040
(6) Make sure that the flight control switches, on the P5 flight control panel, are set to the OFF
position.
SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-045
(7) Make sure that the engine pump switch, for the applicable system, is in the ON position.
SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-046
WARNING
KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT .
(8) Dry-motor the applicable engine to pressurize the hydraulic system
(TASK 71-00-00-700-821-F00).
(a) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure becomes stable between 2800 psi (19,305 kPa) to
3200 psi (22,063 kPa).
NOTE: You can view the hydraulic pressure, for the applicable system, on the display
unit for the engine display.
SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-047
(9) Set the engine pump switch, for the applicable engine, to the OFF position until the hydraulic
pressure decreases to 200 psi (1379 kPa) or less.
NOTE: To accelerate pressure decay, it is acceptable to exercise flight controls to relieve
residual, high pressure as long as safety precautions are observed.
SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-048
(10) Set the engine pump switch, for the applicable system, to the ON position and make sure that
the pressure becomes stable between 2800 psi (19,305 kPa) to 3200 psi (22,063 kPa).
SUBTASK 29-11-11-860-041
(11) Set the engine pump switch, for the applicable system, to the OFF position and let the system
pressure decrease to 200 psi (1379 kPa) or less.
NOTE: To accelerate pressure decay, it is acceptable to exercise flight controls to relieve
residual, high pressure as long as safety precautions are observed.
SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-049
(12) Stop the engine (TASK 71-00-00-700-819-F00).
29-11-11
SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-050
(13) Make sure that the pump does not have a hydraulic leak.
E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-051
(1) Set the flight control switches, on the P5 flight control panel, to the ON position.
SUBTASK 29-11-11-710-052
(2) Set the engine pump switch, for the applicable system, to the ON position.
SUBTASK 29-11-11-840-005
(3) Remove power from the applicable hydraulic system (TASK 29-11-00-860-805).
SUBTASK 29-11-11-860-042
(4) If it is necessary, service the system A and B reservoirs (TASK 12-12-00-610-801).

SUBTASK 29-11-27-020-002
(1) Remove the mounting clamp [4].
(a) Remove the bolts [3].
SUBTASK 29-11-27-480-002

SUBTASK 29-11-27-020-003
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU CAREFULLY DRAIN HYDRAULIC FLUID INTO A
SUITABLE CONTAINER. CAREFULLY CLEAN, DRY , AND DISPOSE OF ALL
LEAKAGE. HYDRAULIC FLUID CAUSES DAMAGE TO RUBBER, COPPER,
PLASTICS, PAINTS, AND MANY OTHER MATERIALS.
(3) Disconnect the pressure line [6] from the acoustic filter [5].
SUBTASK 29-11-27-020-005

SUBTASK 29-11-27-020-004
(5) Remove the acoustic filter [5] from the EMDP [2].
SUBTASK 29-11-27-020-006
(6) If it is necessary, remove the elbow [15] and union [17] from the acoustic filter [5].
(a) Remove and discard the packing [16] and packing [18].
SUBTASK 29-11-27-210-004
(7) To inspect the packing [7], packing [8], and backup rings [9], do these steps:
(a) Remove the filter head [13] from the barrel [12].

ASSEMBLY . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SURFACE OF THE
BARREL AND HEAD ASSEMBLY .
1) Remove and discard the lockwire.

(c) If necessary, remove packing [7], packing [8], and backup rings [9].

F . Acoustic Filter Installation
SUBTASK 29-11-27-420-011
(1) If the packing [7], packing [8], and backup rings [9] were removed, install a new packing [7],
new packing [8], and new backup rings [9].
(a) To install the backup rings [9], do this task: T eflon Backup Rings Installation,
TASK 20-10-31-400-801.
SUBTASK 29-11-27-210-005
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU CORRECTLY ALIGN AND INSTALL BACKUP RINGS.
EXTRUSION AND LEAKS CAN OCCUR IF YOU DO NOT CORRECTLY
INSTALL BACKUP RINGS.
(2) Make sure that the backup rings [9] are aligned and installed correctly.
29-11-27
SUBTASK 29-11-27-420-010
(3) If the filter head [13] was removed, do these steps:
(a) Apply hydraulic fluid, D50122, to the threads of the barrel [12] and filter head [13].
(b) Install the filter head [13] onto the barrel [12].
1) Tighten the filter head [13] to 480 in-lb (54.2 N·m) - 540 in-lb (61.0 N·m).
(c) Apply tamper-proof putty/lacquer, G51751, on the thread connection of the barrel [12]
and filter head [13].
(d) Install MS20995C20 lockwire, G50225, with double twist method
(TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
SUBTASK 29-11-27-100-001
(4) If it is necessary, clean the acoustic filter [5] (TASK 29-11-00-100-801).
SUBTASK 29-11-27-420-009
(5) If the elbow [15] and union [17] are removed, do this task:
(a) Apply hydraulic fluid, D50122, to the threads of the elbow [15] and union [17].
(b) Lubricate the new packing [16] with hydraulic fluid, D50122.
(c) Install the elbow [15] and packing [16] in the acoustic filter [5].
(d) Tighten the elbow [15] at the upper end of the acoustic filter [5] housing to 161.5 in-lb
(18.2 N·m) - 178.5 in-lb (20.2 N·m).
(e) Lubricate the new packing [18] with hydraulic fluid, D50122.
(f) Install the union [17] and packing [18] in the acoustic filter [5].
(g) Tighten the union [17] at the lower end of the acoustic filter [5] housing to 266 in-lb
(30.1 N·m) - 294 in-lb (33.2 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-11-27-420-001
(6) Put the acoustic filter [5] in its mounting position on the EMDP [2].
SUBTASK 29-11-27-420-007
(7) Install the mounting clamp [4].
(a) Put the mounting clamp [4] in its position.
(b) Install the bolts [3].
SUBTASK 29-11-27-420-002
(8) Connect the acoustic filter [5] to the union [19] of the EMDP [2].
(a) Tighten the swivel nut [11] to 665 in-lb (75.1 N·m) - 735 in-lb (83.0 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-11-27-420-004
(9) Connect the pressure line [6] to the acoustic filter [5].
(a) Tighten the pressure line [6] to 475 in-lb (53.7 N·m) - 525 in-lb (59.3 N·m).
NOTE: For hydraulic system A acoustic filter only, position the pressure line so that it provides
the maximum clearance between the pressure line and the filter bowl clamp on the
system A return filter module.
29-11-27
SUBTASK 29-11-27-420-005
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT BEFORE YOU
INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . IF TOO MUCH
TORQUE IS NECESSARY , DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT ,
AND MAKE SURE THAT THE POPPET IS STRAIGHT . AFTER YOU INSTALL IT ,
MAKE SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 IN.
(1.52 MM). IF THE INDICATOR PINS ARE NOT CORRECTLY EXTENDED,
FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR STOP . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
THE RESERVOIR, AND THE PUMP .
(10) Connect the supply line [10] at the quick-disconnect [1].
SUBTASK 29-11-27-860-004
(11) Pressurize the applicable Hydraulic System A or B reservoir (TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or
TASK 29-09-00-860-807).
SUBTASK 29-11-27-860-005
WARNING
WHEN YOU OPEN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS, MAKE SURE THAT THE
OUTER DOOR STAYS AS OPEN AS POSSIBLE. IF THE OUTER DOOR
TURNS IN, THE ATTACHED DOOR COMPONENTS COULD TOUCH THE
INNER DOOR COMPONENTS. THIS CAN CAUSE AN ARC CONDITION
WHEN YOU SUPPLY POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTORS IN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS. BE
CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE
INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS POSSIBLE,
REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST . THE P91 AND P92
PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE
AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES.
(12) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers:

SUBTASK 29-11-31-210-001
(1) Make sure that the surfaces of the system A reservoir [3] are clean.
SUBTASK 29-11-31-210-002
(2) Make sure that unwanted material does not get in the reservoir [3].
SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-001
(3) If it is necessary to install components on the replacement reservoir [3], do these steps:
(a) Install the drain valve [17]:
1) Remove the caps from the ports on the reservoir [3].
2) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054 or hydraulic fluid, D00153 on the new packing [7].
3) Install the packing [7] in the groove of the flange of the drain valve [17].
4) Put the drain valve [17] on the flange.
5) Install the bolts [15] and washers [16].
6) Install the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51674, on the two
bolts [15] with double twist method (TASK 20-10-44-400-801 or
TASK 20-10-44-400-802).
29-11-31
7) Put the drain valve handle in the CLOSED position.
8) Install the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51674, on the
handle of the drain valve [17] and on the other two bolts [15] with double twist
method (TASK 20-10-44-400-801 or TASK 20-10-44-400-802).
(b) Install the reducer [14], reducer [20], and disconnect coupling [8].
1) Remove the caps from the ports on the reservoir [3].
2) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054 or hydraulic fluid, D00153 to the new packing [10],
new packing [13], new packing [19], reducer [14], reducer [20], and disconnect
coupling [8].
3) Install the packing [10], packing [13], packing [19], reducer [14], reducer [20], and
disconnect coupling [8] in the reservoir ports.
(c) Do this task: Hydraulic Fluid Quantity Transmitter/Indicator Installation,
TASK 29-33-12-400-801.

E. Prepare for Installation
SUBTASK 29-11-31-210-003
(1) Make sure that the surfaces of the system B reservoir [23] are clean.
SUBTASK 29-11-31-210-004
(2) Make sure that unwanted material does not get in the system B reservoir [23].
29-11-31
SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-008
(3) If it is necessary to install components on the replacement reservoir [23], do these steps:
(a) Install the drain valve [27]:
1) Remove the caps from the ports on the reservoir [23].
2) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, on the new packing [26].
3) Install the packing [26] in the groove of the flange of the drain valve [27].
4) Put the drain valve [27] on the flange.
5) Install the bolts [29] and washers [28].
6) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51674, on the two
bolts [29] with double twist method (TASK 20-10-44-400-801 or
TASK 20-10-44-400-802).
7) Put the drain valve handle in the CLOSED position.
8) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51674, on the handle
of the drain valve [27] and on the other two bolts [29] with double twist method
(TASK 20-10-44-400-801 or TASK 20-10-44-400-802).
(b) Install the reducer [35], reducer [41], union [30], and union [38].
1) Remove the caps from the ports on the reservoir [23].
2) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054 or hydraulic fluid, D00153 to the new packing [31],
new packing [34], new packing [37], new packing [40], reducer [35], reducer [41],
union [30], and union [38].
3) Install the packing [31], packing [34], packing [37], packing [40], union [30],
union [38], reducer [35], and reducer [41].
(c) Do this task: Hydraulic Fluid Quantity Transmitter/Indicator Installation,
TASK 29-33-12-400-801.
F . Hydraulic System B Reservoir Installation
SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-009
(1) Put the hydraulic system B reservoir [23] in its mounting position.
SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-010
(2) Install the bolts [24] and washers [25].
SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-011
(3) Remove the caps from the electrical connector [42], fluid quantity transmitter, hydraulic
line [32], hydraulic line [33], hydraulic line [36], hydraulic line [39], hydraulic line [43] and the
ports on the reservoir [23].
SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-012
(4) Connect the electrical connector [42] to the fluid quantity transmitter.
SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-013
(5) Connect the hydraulic line [32] to the reservoir [23].
SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-018
(6) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [32] to a torque of 750 ±38 in-lb (84.7 ±4.3 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-019
(7) Connect the hydraulic line [33] to the hydraulic reservoir [23].
SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-020
(8) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [33] to a torque of 360 ±18 in-lb (40.7 ±2.0 N·m).
29-11-31
SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-021
(9) Connect the hydraulic line [36] and hydraulic line [43] to the reservoir [23].
SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-022
(10) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [36] and hydraulic line [43] to a torque of 450 ±23 in-lb
(50.8 ±2.6 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-023
(11) Connect the hydraulic line [39] to the reservoir [23].
SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-024
(12) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [39] to a torque of 280 ±14 in-lb (31.6 ±1.6 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-11-31-420-014
(13) Connect the reservoir pressurization line [22].
SUBTASK 29-11-31-860-010
(14) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2
Row Col Number Name
D 5 C01359 DISPLAY DEU 1 PRI
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1
Row Col Number Name
D 11 C01360 DISPLAY DEU 2 PRI

SUBTASK 29-11-31-610-002
(1) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801.
SUBTASK 29-11-31-860-006
(2) Pressurize the hydraulic system B reservoir (TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or
TASK 29-09-00-860-807).
SUBTASK 29-11-31-790-002
(3) Do a check for leaks.
SUBTASK 29-11-31-930-004
(4) Remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tags from the hydraulic pump switches.

F . EMDP Case Drain Filter Element Removal
SUBTASK 29-11-41-020-018
(1) If it is necessary, remove the filter module, do this task: EMDP Case Drain Filter Module
Removal, TASK 29-11-41-000-802.
NOTE: The filter element can be removed from the filter module after removing the module
from the airplane.
29-11-41
SUBTASK 29-11-41-020-001
(2) Remove the lockwire or safety cable from the filter bowl [13] (TASK 20-10-44-000-801 or
TASK 20-10-44-000-802).
SUBTASK 29-11-41-020-017
(3) Remove the filter bowl [13] from the filter head.
(a) Put a container below the filter bowl [13] to catch any hydraulic fluid.
SUBTASK 29-11-41-020-002
(4) Remove the filter element [12] from the case drain filter assembly [6].
SUBTASK 29-11-41-020-003
(5) Remove the packing [9] from the filter element [12].
(a) Discard the packing [9].
SUBTASK 29-11-41-020-004
(6) Remove the packing [11] and backup rings [10] from the filter head.
NOTE: An o-ring pick, COM-7293, may be used to remove the packing.
(a) Make sure that you do not scratch the filter head.
(b) Discard the packing [11].
(c) If you find a crack, damage or deformation on any backup rings [10], discard the part.
SUBTASK 29-11-41-210-008
(7) Check the EMDP for condition every time when the filter is removed (EMDP Case Drain Filter
Element and Bowl Inspection, TASK 29-11-41-200-801).
SUBTASK 29-11-41-140-001
(8) Clean the filter bowl [13].

D. Procedure
SUBTASK 29-11-41-170-001
(1) Flush the hydraulic lines between the case drain filter and the hydraulic pump.
SUBTASK 29-11-41-210-004
(2) Look for metal contamination in the pressure filter for the EMDP , do this task: Hydraulic
Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Removal, TASK 29-11-71-000-802.
(a) If you find metal contamination, do these steps:
1) Flush the hydraulic lines between the pressure filter and the EMDP .
2) Install a new pressure filter element.
These are the tasks: Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element
Removal, TASK 29-11-71-000-802, Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module
Filter Element Installation, TASK 29-11-71-400-802.
3) Install a new EMDP .
29-11-41
These are the tasks: Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Removal,
TASK 29-11-21-000-801-001, Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Installation,
TASK 29-11-21-400-801-001.
(b) If you do not find metal contamination in the pressure filter of the EMDP , do this task:
Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Installation,
TASK 29-11-71-400-802.
SUBTASK 29-11-41-210-005
(3) Look for metal contamination in the acoustic filter for the EMDP , do this task: Hydraulic
Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Removal,
TASK 29-11-27-000-801.
(a) If you find metal contamination, do these steps:
1) Clean the acoustic filter, do this task: Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric
Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Cleaning, TASK 29-11-00-100-801.
2) Install a new EMDP .
These are the tasks: Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Removal,
TASK 29-11-21-000-801-001, Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Installation,
TASK 29-11-21-400-801-001.
(b) If you do not find metal contamination in the acoustic filter, do this task: Hydraulic
Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter Installation,
TASK 29-11-27-400-801.
SUBTASK 29-11-41-210-006
(4) If the acoustic filter and the pressure filter for the EMDP do not have metal contamination, then
do these steps:
(a) Look for metal contamination in the pressure filter for the PTU, do this task: PTU
Pressure Filter Element - Removal, TASK 29-22-21-020-801.
(b) If you find metal contamination, do these steps:
1) Flush the hydraulic lines between the pressure filter and the PTU.
2) Install a new PTU pressure filter element.
These are the tasks: PTU Pressure Filter Element - Removal,
TASK 29-22-21-020-801, PTU Pressure Filter Element - Installation,
TASK 29-22-21-400-802.
3) Install a new PTU.
These are the tasks: Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Removal, TASK 29-22-11-000-801,
Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Installation, TASK 29-22-11-400-801.
(c) If the pressure filter for the PTU does not have metal contamination, do these steps:
1) Do this task: Power Transfer Unit (PTU) System Test, TASK 29-22-00-730-801.
2) If the PTU does not operate correctly, replace the PTU.
These are the tasks: Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Removal, TASK 29-22-11-000-801,
Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Installation, TASK 29-22-11-400-801.

C. Prepare for the Inspection
SUBTASK 29-11-41-020-015
(1) Do this task: EMDP Case Drain Filter Element Removal, TASK 29-11-41-000-801.
D. Inspection
SUBTASK 29-11-41-211-001
(1) Examine the filter element, the filter bowl, and the fluid in the filter bowl for metal
contamination.
(a) If you find a small quantity of metal particles that have equal dimensions, do these steps:
NOTE: It is not necessary to replace a pump if the quantity of metal particles is small and
they have equal dimensions. The filter can have more particles during initial
operation of a new pump while mating parts wear away small surface defects. It
is not necessary to replace the pump if more small particles are found at the next
filter change after installation of a new pump.
1) Replace the filter element.
2) Do this task: HYDRAULIC SYSTEMS A AND B - ADJUSTMENT/TEST ,
PAGEBLOCK 29-11-00/501.
3) Examine the filter again at the next scheduled filter change interval.
(b) If you find a large quantity of small metal particles, large metal particles that are not of
equal dimensions, or a large quantity of steel particles, do these steps:
NOTE: A large quantity of small metal particles, or large metal particles that are not of
equal dimensions, can be an indication of an unsatisfactory pump. The particles
are usually bronze mixed with a small quantity of steel. A large quantity of steel
particles is an indication of unsatisfactorily worn bearings.
29-11-41
1) Replace the pump at the next maintenance opportunity
(TASK 29-11-21-000-801-001 and TASK 29-11-21-400-801-001).
2) Write down the results of the filter inspection and give them to the pump overhaul
facility.
NOTE: The filter inspection results can be used as an aid to find the condition of
the pump. A pump with an unsatisfactory bearing can pass the functional
test and be returned to service with no fault found. Giving the filter
inspection data to the overhaul facility can prevent the return of an
unsatisfactory pump to service.
3) Replace the filter element.
CAUTION
FLUSH THE HYDRAULIC LINES TO REMOVE METAL CONTAMINATION.
IF A LARGE QUANTITY OF METAL CONTAMINATION STAYS IN THE
LINES, THE FILTER CAN BECOME BLOCKED. A BLOCKED FILTER CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE PUMP .
(c) If you will remove a pump because of metal contamination in the filter, flush the hydraulic
lines and replace the applicable filter elements (TASK 29-11-00-170-801).
SUBTASK 29-11-41-210-007
(2) Inspect the filter element for damages.
(a) Discard and replace the filter element if damages are found.

(1) Do this task: EMDP Case Drain Filter Element Installation, TASK 29-11-41-400-801.

SUBTASK 29-11-51-020-019
CAUTION
DO NOT DISCONNECT THE QUICK-RELEASE FITTING FOR THE
HYDRAULIC CASE DRAIN-LINE AT THE SUPPORT BEAM FOR THE STRUT
FAN COWL. A DISCONNECTED CASE DRAIN LINE WITH A QUICK-RELEASE
FITTING CAN CAUSE TO INCORRECT INSTALLATION. AN INCORRECTLY
INSTALLED QUICK-RELEASE FITTING CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
HYDRAULIC PUMP .
(1) Do not disconnect the hydraulic case drain line quick release fitting at the strut fan cowl
support beam.
NOTE: It is not necessary to disconnect the hydraulic case drain line quick release fitting. A
check valve is installed on the downstream side of the Engine Driven Pump (EDP)
case drain filter module. The check valve will prevent hydraulic fluid loss when the
EDP case drain filter element is removed.
SUBTASK 29-11-51-000-002

module, do these tasks:
29-11-51
• EDP Case Drain Filter Module Removal, TASK 29-11-51-000-802
• EDP Case Drain Filter Module Installation, TASK 29-11-51-400-802.
SUBTASK 29-11-51-020-021
(3) Remove the lockwire or safety cable from the filter bowl [8] (TASK 20-10-44-000-801 or
TASK 20-10-44-000-802).
SUBTASK 29-11-51-020-001
(4) Remove the filter bowl [8] from the filter head.
(a) Drain the hydraulic fluid into a container.
SUBTASK 29-11-51-020-012
(5) Remove the filter element [7] from the filter head.
SUBTASK 29-11-51-020-013
(6) Remove the packing [6] from the filter element [7].
(a) Discard the packing [6].
SUBTASK 29-11-51-020-014
(7) Remove the packing [10] and backup rings [5] from the filter head.
NOTE: You can use an o-ring pick, COM-7293, to remove the packing.
(a) Discard the packing [10].
(b) If you find a crack, damage or deformation on a backup ring [5], discard the part.
SUBTASK 29-11-51-210-007

D. Inspection
SUBTASK 29-11-51-211-001
(1) Examine the filter element, the filter bowl, and the fluid in the filter bowl for metal
contamination.
(a) If you find a small quantity of metal particles that have equal dimensions, do these steps:
NOTE: It is not necessary to replace a pump if the quantity of metal particles is small and
they have equal dimensions. The filter can have more particles during initial
operation of a new pump while mating parts wear away small surface defects. It
is not necessary to replace the pump if more small particles are found at the next
filter change after installation of a new pump.
1) Replace the filter element.
2) Do an operational test of the engine driven pump (TASK 29-11-00-700-801).
3) Examine the filter again at the next scheduled filter change interval.
29-11-51
(b) If you find a large quantity of small metal particles, large metal particles that are not of
equal dimensions, or a large quantity of steel particles, do these steps:
NOTE: A large quantity of small metal particles, or large metal particles that are not of
equal dimensions, can be an indication of an unsatisfactory pump. The particles
are usually bronze mixed with a small quantity of steel. A large quantity of steel
particles is an indication of unsatisfactorily worn bearings.
1) Replace the pump at the next maintenance opportunity
(TASK 29-11-11-000-801-001 and TASK 29-11-11-400-801-001).
2) Write down the results of the filter inspection and give them to the pump overhaul
facility.
NOTE: The filter inspection results can be used as an aid to find the condition of
the pump. A pump with an unsatisfactory bearing can pass the functional
test and be returned to service with no fault found. Giving the filter
inspection data to the overhaul facility can prevent the return of an
unsatisfactory pump to service.
3) Replace the filter element.
CAUTION
FLUSH THE HYDRAULIC LINES TO REMOVE METAL CONTAMINATION.
IF A LARGE QUANTITY OF METAL CONTAMINATION STAYS IN THE
LINES, THE FILTER CAN BECOME BLOCKED. A BLOCKED FILTER CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE PUMP .
(c) If you will remove a pump because of metal contamination in the filter, flush the hydraulic
lines and replace the applicable filter elements (TASK 29-11-00-170-801).
SUBTASK 29-11-51-210-005
(2) Inspect the filter element for damages.
(a) Discard and replace the filter element if damages are found.

CAUTION

F . Bulkhead Fittings to Spar and Hydraulic Lines - Bonding Resistance Check
SUBTASK 29-11-55-760-003
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE BONDING RESISTANCE IS LESS THAN THE LIMITS.
THE RESISTANCE OF THE ELECTRICAL BOND IS VERY IMPORTANT IF
LIGHTNING HITS THE AIRPLANE. AN EXPLOSION CAN OCCUR IF THE
BONDING RESISTANCE IS NOT IN THE LIMITS DURING A LIGHTNING
STRIKE.
(1) For the bulkhead fitting [1] to the rear spar [2] outside the fuel tank resistance, do these steps:
(a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550
(b) Make sure that the electrical fay surface bond resistance between the bulkhead fitting [1]
and the rear spar [2] outside the fuel tank is 0.0010 ohm (1.0 milli-ohm) or less (SWPM
20-20-00).
(c) If the resistance is above the specified value, loosen the bulkhead fittings to repair the
electrical bond:
1) Do this task: Bulkhead Fittings - Separate From Rear Spar to Repair Electrical
Bond, TASK 29-11-55-300-801.
29-11-55
SUBTASK 29-11-55-760-004
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE BONDING RESISTANCE IS LESS THAN THE LIMITS.
THE RESISTANCE OF THE ELECTRICAL BOND IS VERY IMPORTANT IF
LIGHTNING HITS THE AIRPLANE. AN EXPLOSION CAN OCCUR IF THE
BONDING RESISTANCE IS NOT IN THE LIMITS DURING A LIGHTNING
STRIKE.
(2) For the bulkhead fitting [1] to the hydraulic tube inside the fuel tank resistance, do these steps:
(a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550
(b) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance between the hydraulic tube in the fuel
tank and bulkhead fitting [1] is 0.00050 ohm (0.50 milli-ohm) or less.
(c) Remove and install a new hydraulic tube to the bulkhead fitting [1], if the resistance is
above the specified value.

G. Separate the Bulkhead Fittings from the Rear Spar
SUBTASK 29-11-55-100-001
CAUTION
DO NOT LET HYDRAULIC FLUID GET ON EQUIPMENT . IF HYDRAULIC
FLUID GETS ON EQUIPMENT , IMMEDIATELY CLEAN IT FROM THE
EQUIPMENT . HYDRAULIC FLUID CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT .
(1) During this procedure, if you get hydraulic fluid on any equipment, surfaces or cables, clean it
off immediately, do this task: Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane,
TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane,
TASK 12-40-00-100-803
SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-007
CAUTION
USE TWO WRENCHES TO DISCONNECT OR CONNECT TUBES. IF YOU DO
NOT USE A WRENCH ON EACH SIDE OF THE CONNECTION, DAMAGE TO
THE TUBES CAN OCCUR.
(2) Disconnect the hydraulic tube B-nuts attached to the inlet and outlet bulkhead fittings [2] on the
outside of the fuel tank.
(a) Drain the hydraulic fluid into a oil resistant container, STD-203.
(b) Install plugs in the disconnected hydraulic tubes [1] and caps on the bulkhead fittings [2]
to prevent contamination.
SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-008
(3) If necessary, remove any support clamps or blocks from the disconnected hydraulic tubes [1]
to allow the bulkhead fittings [2] to be pulled away from the rear spar [3].
SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-009
(4) Do these steps to loosen the bulkhead fittings [2] from the rear spar [3]:
(a) Remove the sealant from the bulkhead fittings [2], two sides of the rear spar [3], and
bolts [4] with the scraper, STD-6401, or scraper, STD-11161.
NOTE: Remove sealant with cutting tools or spatulas made from fiberglass, hardwood,
or plastic. Use only metal tools for the sealant removal on metal structures.
NOTE: The unions can stay installed on their bulkhead fittings.
(b) Remove the collars [6] from the bolts [4] (SRM 51-40-02-0G-0).
SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-010
(5) Remove the fuel tubes adjacent to hydraulic tubes in the fuel tank if necessary to get access to
the heat exchanger and related hydraulic tubing, do this task: Fuel Line, Fitting and Coupling
Removal, TASK 28-22-15-000-801.
SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-011
(6) Disconnect the clamps [7] from the tank structure, on the hydraulic lines from the heat
exchanger to the bulkhead fittings.
29-11-55
SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-012
(7) Do these steps to loosen the applicable heat exchanger [8] from the attach points in the main
fuel tank:
(a) Remove the nuts [9], washers [10], washers [11], and bolts [12] from the heat
exchanger [8] at two diagonal locations.
(b) Remove the nut [13], washer [14], washer [15], bolt [16], and washer [17] that attach the
heat exchanger [8] to the tank.
(c) Remove the nut [13], washer [14], bolt [18], washer [15], bonding jumper [19],
washer [20], and washer [17] that attach the heat exchanger [8] to the tank.
(d) Keep a record of the number of washers [17] for installation.
SUBTASK 29-11-55-020-013
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU ARE CAREFUL WHEN YOU DISCONNECT THE
BULKHEAD FITTINGS FROM THE REAR SPAR. YOU MUST KEEP THE
O-RINGS SERVICEABLE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , YOU MUST REPLACE THE
BULKHEAD FITTINGS.
(8) Carefully move the heat exchanger [8] and connected hydraulic tubing aft to disconnect the
bulkhead fittings [2] from the rear spar [3].
H. Prepare for the Installation
SUBTASK 29-11-55-100-002
(1) Clean unwanted material from the O-ring [21] with cotton wiper, G00034.
SUBTASK 29-11-55-200-001
(2) Examine the condition of the O-ring [21] on each bulkhead fitting [2].
(a) If the O-ring [21] is damaged, replace the bulkhead fitting [2], do these tasks:
• Bulkhead Fitting Removal, TASK 29-11-55-000-801
• Bulkhead Fitting Installation, TASK 29-11-55-400-801.
SUBTASK 29-11-55-160-008
(3) Do the prepare for installation steps of task: Bulkhead Fitting Installation,
TASK 29-11-55-400-801.
(a) Carefully move the O-ring [21] if necessary during cleaning.
SUBTASK 29-11-55-160-009
(4) Prepare the heat exchanger, bonding jumper terminal, and washer below the terminal for
category 1 bonding (unsealed) (SWPM 20-20-00 and 20-20-10).
SUBTASK 29-11-55-160-005
(5) Clean the heat exchanger, bonding jumper terminal, and washer below the terminal with cotton
wiper, G00034, and alcohol, B00065.
29-11-55
SUBTASK 29-11-55-370-008
WARNING
DO NOT GET THE ALODINE SOLUTION IN YOUR MOUTH, IN YOUR EYES,
ON YOUR SKIN, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES
FROM THIS MATERIAL. AIR MUST FLOW FREELY THROUGH THE WORK-
AREA. USE THE NECESSARY RESPIRATORY PROTECTION. KEEP THIS
MATERIAL AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . THIS MATERIAL IS
POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT .
(6) Manually apply Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C50315, to any bare aluminum.

time.

E. Return Filter Module Removal
SUBTASK 29-11-61-020-008
(1) Do this step to remove system A filter module [8]:
RYR 285-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; AIRPLANES WITH THREADED
FILTER MODULE
(a) Remove the lockwire on the reducer [6] in port 2 and on the union [5] in port 3
(TASK 20-10-44-000-801).
RYR ALL
29-11-61
(b) Disconnect the hydraulic line [3], hydraulic line [4] and disconnect the port 1 union [5]
from the hydraulic line.
SUBTASK 29-11-61-020-009
(2) Do this step to remove system B filter module [13]:
RYR 285-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; AIRPLANES WITH THREADED
FILTER MODULE
(a) Remove the lockwire on the plug [17] in port 2 and on the union [5] in port 3
(TASK 20-10-44-000-801).
RYR ALL
(b) Disconnect the hydraulic line [12], and disconnect the union [5] from the port 1 hydraulic
line.
SUBTASK 29-11-61-020-010
(3) Install plugs in the disconnected hydraulic lines.
SUBTASK 29-11-61-680-001
(4) Drain the hydraulic fluid into a 1 gallon (3.8 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-6569.
SUBTASK 29-11-61-160-001
(5) If it is necessary, do this task: Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane,
TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane,
TASK 12-40-00-100-803.
SUBTASK 29-11-61-020-011
(6) Remove the bolts [1] and washers [2].
SUBTASK 29-11-61-020-012
(7) Remove the filter module [8] and/or filter module [13].

E. Return Filter Module Installation
SUBTASK 29-11-61-420-002
(1) Install the filter module [8] and/or filter module [13].
(a) If packings and fittings are not installed on the filter module, do these steps:
1) For system A filter module [8]:
a) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new
packings [7], unions [5] and reducer [6].
b) Install the new packing [7] and union [5] in port 1, new packing [7] and
reducer [6] in port 2, and new packing [7] and union [5] in port 3.
RYR 285-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; AIRPLANES WITH THREADED
FILTER MODULE
c) Install the lockwire on the reducer [6] in port 2 and on the union [5] in port 3
(TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
RYR ALL
2) For system B filter module [13] do these steps:
a) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new
packings [7], unions [5] and port 2 plug [17].
b) Install the new packing [7] and union [5] in port 1, new packing [7] and
union [5] in port 3, and new packing [7] and plug [17] in port 2.
RYR 285-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; AIRPLANES WITH THREADED
FILTER MODULE
c) Install lockwire on the plug [17] in port 2 and on the union [5] in port 3
(TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
RYR ALL
(b) Attach the filter module [8] or filter module [13] to the structure with bolts [1] and
washers [2].
(c) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic lines.
(d) For the filter module [8] connect the hydraulic line [3] to port 3, connect the hydraulic
line [4] to port 2 and connect the union [5] in port 1 to the hydraulic line.
(e) For the filter module [13] connect the hydraulic line [12] to port 3, and connect the
union [5] in port 1 to the hydraulic line.
(f) For the system A filter module [8] only:
1) Loosen the nut [10] from the clamp [9].
2) Position the clamp [9] so that the opening of the clamp is inboard and the nut [10] is
accessible, providing the maximum clearance from the system A Electric
Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) pressure hose.
3) Tighten the nut [10] on the clamp [9] to 120 in-lb (13.6 N·m) - 144 in-lb (16.3 N·m)
(for filter assembly from Aircraft Porus Media manufacturer), or 60 in-lb (6.8 N·m) -
70 in-lb (7.9 N·m) (for filter assembly from Purolator manufacturer).

WHEN YOU SUPPLY POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTORS IN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS. BE
CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON
THE INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS
POSSIBLE, REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST . THE P91
AND P92 PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS.
ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE
INJURIES.

F . Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Removal
SUBTASK 29-11-71-440-001
(1) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-001
(2) Disconnect the applicable hydraulic system electrical connectors from the pressure switches
and the pressure transducer:
(a) Hydraulic System A: Disconnect the electrical connector [1], electrical connector [2], and
electrical connector [3].
(b) Hydraulic System B: Disconnect the electrical connector [1], electrical connector [2],
electrical connector [3], and electrical connector [31].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-002
(3) Disconnect the applicable hydraulic system hydraulic lines, do this task: Flareless Tubing
Assembly Removal, TASK 20-10-51-000-801.
(a) Hydraulic System A: Disconnect the hydraulic line [10], hydraulic line [13], hydraulic
line [20], hydraulic line [24], hydraulic line [27], and hydraulic line [30].
(b) Hydraulic System B: Disconnect the hydraulic line [10], hydraulic line [13], hydraulic
line [20], hydraulic line [24], and hydraulic line [27].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-680-001
(4) Drain hydraulic fluid into a 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-160-001
(5) Do this task: Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-801
or Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-803.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-003
(6) Install plugs to the hydraulic lines on the applicable hydraulic system to prevent contamination
and damage:
29-11-71
(a) Hydraulic System A: Install plugs to the hydraulic line [10], hydraulic line [13], hydraulic
line [20], hydraulic line [24], hydraulic line [27], and hydraulic line [30] to prevent
contamination or damage.
(b) Hydraulic System B: Install plugs to the hydraulic line [10], hydraulic line [13], hydraulic
line [20], hydraulic line [24], and hydraulic line [27] to prevent contamination or damage.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-021
(7) Remove the lockwire between applicable plug and pressure module [57]:
(a) For the Hydraulic System A, remove the lockwire between the plug [6] and pressure
module [57].
(b) For the Hydraulic System B, remove the lockwire between the plug [32] and pressure
module [57].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-004
(8) Remove the unions and the plug from the pressure module [57] on the applicable hydraulic
system:
(a) Hydraulic System A: Remove the union [8], union [11], union [18], union [22], union [25],
union [28], and plug [6] from the pressure module [57].
1) Discard the packing [7], packing [9], packing [12], packing [19], packing [23],
packing [26], and packing [29].
(b) Hydraulic System B: Remove the union [8], union [11], union [18], union [22], union [25],
and plug [32] from the pressure module [57].
1) Discard the packing [9], packing [12], packing [19], packing [23], packing [26], and
packing [33].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-001
(9) Install plugs in the open ports of the pressure module [57] to prevent contamination or
damage.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-005
(10) Remove the bolt [4], bolt [14], washer [5], and washer [15].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-006
(11) Remove the pressure module [57].

G. Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Installation
SUBTASK 29-11-71-210-001
CAUTION
DO NOT LET UNWANTED MATERIALS GO INTO THE PRESSURE MODULE
OR THE HYDRAULIC LINES. DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(1) Make sure that unwanted material does not go into the pressure module ports or the hydraulic
lines.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-640-001
(2) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packings and to the
threads of the plug and union for the applicable hydraulic system.
(a) Hydraulic System A: Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the
new packing [7], packing [9], packing [12], packing [19], packing [23], packing [26], and
packing [29] and to the threads of the plug [6], union [8], union [11], union [18], union [22],
union [25], and union [28].
(b) Hydraulic System B: Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the
new packing [9], packing [12], packing [19], packing [23], packing [26], and packing [33]
and to the threads of the union [8], union [11], union [18], union [22], union [25], and
plug [32].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-002
(3) Install the new packings on the plug and unions for the applicable hydraulic system.
(a) For Hydraulic System A, do these steps:
1) Install the new packing [7] on the plug [6].
2) Install the new packing [9] to the union [8].
3) Install the new packing [12] on the union [11].
29-11-71
4) Install the new packing [19] on the union [18].
5) Install the new packing [23] on the union [22].
6) Install the new packing [26] on the union [25].
7) Install the new packing [29] on the union [28].
(b) For Hydraulic System B, do these steps:
1) Install the new packing [9] on the union [8].
2) Install the new packing [12] on the union [11].
3) Install the new packing [19] on the union [18].
4) Install the new packing [23] on the union [22].
5) Install the new packing [26] on the union [25].
6) Install the new packing [33] on the plug [32].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-010-001
(4) If shipping plugs are in ports of the pressure module [57], remove them.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-210-002
(5) Install the plug and unions in the pressure module [57] for the applicable hydraulic system.
(a) Hydraulic System A: Install the plug [6], union [8], union [11], union [18], union [22],
union [25], and union [28] in the correct ports of the pressure module [57].
1) Tighten the union [8] to 280 ±14 in-lb (32 ±2 N·m).
2) Tighten the union [11] to 360 ±18 in-lb (41 ±2 N·m).
3) Tighten the union [18] to 450 ±23 in-lb (51 ±3 N·m).
4) Tighten the union [22] to 360 ±18 in-lb (41 ±2 N·m).
5) Tighten the union [25] to 450 ±23 in-lb (51 ±3 N·m).
6) Tighten the union [28] to 280 ±14 in-lb (32 ±2 N·m).
NOTE: For installation torque values, refer to Standard Torque Values,
TASK 20-50-11-910-801.
(b) Hydraulic System B: Install the union [8], union [11], union [18], union [22], union [25], and
plug [32] in the correct ports of the pressure module [57].
1) Tighten the union [8] to 280 ±14 in-lb (32 ±2 N·m).
2) Tighten the union [11] to 360 ±18 in-lb (41 ±2 N·m).
3) Tighten the union [18] to 450 ±23 in-lb (51 ±3 N·m).
4) Tighten the union [22] to 360 ±18 in-lb (41 ±2 N·m).
5) Tighten the union [25] to 450 ±23 in-lb (51 ±3 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-11-71-210-003
(6) Make sure that the check valves [21] are installed in the pressure module [57].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-003
(7) Put the pressure module pressure module [57] in its mounting position.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-004
(8) Install the bolt [4], bolt [14], washer [5], and washer [15].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-760-001
(9) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the pressure module [57] and bracket
(SWPM 20-20-00).
29-11-71
(a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
(b) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.001 ohm (1.0 milliohm) or less.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-007
(10) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic lines on the applicable hydraulic system.
(a) Hydraulic System A: Remove the plugs from the hydraulic line [10], hydraulic line [13],
hydraulic line [20], hydraulic line [24], hydraulic line [27], and hydraulic line [30].
(b) Hydraulic System B: Remove the plugs from the hydraulic line [10], hydraulic line [13],
hydraulic line [20], hydraulic line [24], and hydraulic line [27].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-005
(11) Connect the hydraulic lines to the pressure module [57] on the applicable hydraulic system, do
this task: Flareless Tubing Assembly Installation, TASK 20-10-51-400-804.
(a) Hydraulic System A: Connect the hydraulic line [10], hydraulic line [13], hydraulic
line [20], hydraulic line [24], hydraulic line [27], and hydraulic line [30] to the pressure
module [57].
1) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [10] to 700 ±35 in-lb (79 ±4 N·m).
2) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [13] to 500 ±25 in-lb (56 ±3 N·m).
3) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [20] to 450 ±23 in-lb (51 ±3 N·m).
4) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [24] to 900 ±45 in-lb (102 ±5 N·m).
5) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [27] to 700 ±35 in-lb (79 ±4 N·m).
6) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [30] to 500 ±25 in-lb (56 ±3 N·m).
(b) Hydraulic System B: Connect the hydraulic line [10], hydraulic line [13], hydraulic
line [20], hydraulic line [24], and hydraulic line [27] to the pressure module [57].
1) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [10] to 500 ±25 in-lb (56 ±3 N·m).
2) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [13] to 900 ±45 in-lb (102 ±5 N·m).
3) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [20] to 450 ±23 in-lb (51 ±3 N·m).
4) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [24] to 500 ±25 in-lb (56 ±3 N·m).
5) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [27] to 900 ±45 in-lb (102 ±5 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-006
(12) Connect the electrical connectors to the pressure switches and the pressure transducer on the
applicable hydraulic system.
(a) Hydraulic System A: Connect the electrical connector [1], electrical connector [2], and
electrical connector [3] to the pressure switches and pressure transducer.
(b) Hydraulic System B: Connect the electrical connector [1], electrical connector [2],
electrical connector [3], and electrical connector [31] to the pressure switches and
pressure transducer.

SUBTASK 29-11-71-710-001
(5) Do an operational check of the system A pressure module [57].
(a) Make sure that the ENG 1 HYD PUMPS switch, on the P5 panel, is ON position.
(b) Make sure that the ELEC 2 HYD PUMPS switch, on the P5 panel, is OFF position.
(c) Make sure that the ENG 1 and ELEC 2 LOW PRESSURE lights, on the P5 panel, are on.
(d) Pressurize the hydraulic system A with EDP , do this task: Hydraulic System A or B
Pressurization with an Engine-Driven Pump (EDP), TASK 29-11-00-860-804.
(e) Make sure that the ENG 1 LOW PRESSURE light goes off.
(f) Make sure that the ELEC 2 LOW PRESSURE light stays on.
(g) Examine the module and connections for leaks.
(h) Remove hydraulic system A power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power
Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
(i) Operate the rudder until the ENG 1 LOW PRESSURE light comes on.
(j) Pressurize system A with EMDP , do this task: Hydraulic System Pressurization with an
Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP), TASK 29-11-00-860-803.
(k) Make sure that the ELEC 2 LOW PRESSURE light goes off.
(l) Make sure that the ENG 1 LOW PRESSURE light stays on.
(m) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
(n) Make sure that the ELEC 2 LOW PRESSURE light comes on.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-710-002
(6) Do an operational check of system B pressure module [57].
(a) Make sure that the ENG 2 HYD PUMPS switch, on the P5 panel, is ON position.
(b) Make sure that the ELEC 1 HYD PUMPS switch, on the P5 panel, is OFF position.
(c) Make sure that the ENG 2 and ELEC 1 LOW PRESSURE lights, on the P5 panel, are on.
(d) Pressurize the hydraulic system B with EDP , do this task: Hydraulic System A or B
Pressurization with an Engine-Driven Pump (EDP), TASK 29-11-00-860-804.
(e) Make sure that the ENG 2 LOW PRESSURE light goes off.
(f) Make sure that the ELEC 1 LOW PRESSURE light stays on.
(g) Examine the module and connections for leaks.
29-11-71
(h) Remove hydraulic system B power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power
Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
(i) Operate the rudder until the ENG 2 LOW PRESSURE light comes on.
(j) Pressurize the system B with EMDP , do this task: Hydraulic System Pressurization with
an Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP), TASK 29-11-00-860-803.
(k) Make sure that the ELEC 1 LOW PRESSURE light goes off.
(l) Make sure that the ENG 2 LOW PRESSURE light stays on.
(m) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
(n) Make sure that the ELEC 1 LOW PRESSURE light comes on.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-025
(7) For the Hydraulic System A, install lockwire MS20995NC32 between the plug [6] and system A
pressure module [57] with the double-twist method.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-026
(8) For the Hydraulic System B, install lockwire MS20995NC32 between the plug [32] and system
B pressure module [57] with the double-twist method.
I. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 29-11-71-610-001
(1) If it is necessary, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801.

4. Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Removal
(Figure 401)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) There is one pressure modules for each hydraulic system. Each pressure module has two filter
assemblies, one filter is for the electric motor driven pump and the other filter is for the engine
driven pump. The procedure to remove and install each filter is similar.

E. Prepare for the Removal
SUBTASK 29-11-71-860-010
(1) Remove hydraulic power from the applicable system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B

TASK 29-09-00-860-808.
F . Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Removal
SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-016
(1) Remove the lockwire from the filter bowl [16].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-017
CAUTION
PULL DOWN ON THE KNURLED RING OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT
BEFORE YOU TURN IT . IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS, TOO MUCH TORQUE
WILL BE NECESSARY TO TURN THE RING. THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO
THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT .
(2) Disconnect the self-seal (quick) disconnect hose from the applicable hydraulic system reservoir
(TASK 29-11-27-000-801).
SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-008
(3) Remove the filter bowl [16].
(a) Put a container under the filter bowl [16] to catch any hydraulic fluid.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-009
(4) Remove the filter [47].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-160-002
(5) Clean the filter bowl [16].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-010
(6) Remove the packing [43], packing [45], backup rings [46], and backup ring [44].
(a) Discard the packing [43], packing [45], backup rings [46], and backup ring [44].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-210-004
(7) Use a dental mirror, STD-3907, to examine the filter [47] for metal contamination.
(a) If the filter [47] for the Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) contains metal contamination,
do these tasks:
• Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Removal, TASK 29-11-21-000-801-001
• Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Installation, TASK 29-11-21-400-801-001.
29-11-71
(b) If the filter [47] for the Engine-Driven Pump (EDP) contains metal contamination, do these
tasks:
• Hydraulic Systems A and B Engine-Driven Pump (EDP) Removal,
TASK 29-11-11-000-801-001
• Hydraulic Systems A and B Engine-Driven Pump (EDP) Installation,
TASK 29-11-11-400-801-001.
(c) If metal contamination is found in the pressure filter, flush the hydraulic lines between the
pressure module [57] and hydraulic pump that was removed.
(d) If metal contamination is found in the EMDP pressure filter, examine the EMDP acoustic
filter, do these tasks:
• Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter
Removal, TASK 29-11-27-000-801
• Hydraulic Systems A and B Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) Acoustic Filter
Installation, TASK 29-11-27-400-801.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-020-011
(8) Discard the filter [47].

E. Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Installation
SUBTASK 29-11-71-640-002
(1) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [45] and the
new backup rings [46].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-007
(2) Install the new packing [45] and the new backup rings [46] in the groove in the pressure
module [57].
(a) Make sure that you set the new packing [45] and the new backup rings [46] correctly or
they can cause a leak.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-640-003
(3) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [43] and the
new backup ring [44].
29-11-71
SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-008
(4) Install the new packing [43] and the new backup ring [44] in the groove at the top of the new
filter [47] with the new packing [43] at the top.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-640-004
(5) Lightly apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the threads of the filter
bowl [16].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-610-002
(6) Fill the filter bowl [16] approximately one third full with hydraulic fluid, D00153.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-009
(7) Put the new filter [47] in the pressure module [57].
SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-010
(8) Torque the filter bowl [16] to 350 in-lb (39.5 N·m) - 375 in-lb (42.4 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-011
(9) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, between the filter bowl [16] and pressure module [57]
(TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
SUBTASK 29-11-71-420-022
CAUTION
PULL DOWN ON THE KNURLED RING OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT
BEFORE YOU TURN IT . IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS, TOO MUCH TORQUE
WILL BE NECESSARY TO TURN THE RING. THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO
THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT .
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT BEFORE YOU
INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . IF TOO MUCH
TORQUE IS NECESSARY , DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT ,
AND MAKE SURE THAT THE POPPET IS STRAIGHT . AFTER YOU INSTALL IT ,
MAKE SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 IN.
(1.52 MM). IF THE INDICATOR PINS ARE NOT CORRECTLY EXTENDED,
FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR STOP . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
THE RESERVOIR, AND THE PUMP .
(10) Reconnect the self-seal (quick) disconnect hose (TASK 29-11-27-400-801).
F . Hydraulic System A and B Pressure Module Filter Element Installation Test
SUBTASK 29-11-71-600-001
(1) If it is necessary to service the applicable hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir
Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-860-013
(2) Pressurize the applicable hydraulic reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization,
TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-807.
29-11-71
SUBTASK 29-11-71-860-014
WARNING
KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT .
(3) Pressurize the applicable hydraulic system with the applicable hydraulic pump for the installed
filter element:
NOTE: The hydraulic pressure module has one set of hydraulic circuits and filter for the
Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) and one more set for the Engine Driven Pump
(EDP). You must use the correct pump to do the leakage check.
(a) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-790-001
(4) Examine the pressure module [57] for leaks.
SUBTASK 29-11-71-860-015
(5) Remove hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal,
TASK 29-11-00-860-805.

connected to the Engine 2.

SUBTASK 29-11-81-640-001
(1) Lubricate the new packings [5] with MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, and
put them in their positions on the shutoff valve [1].
SUBTASK 29-11-81-420-001
(2) Carefully put the shutoff valve [1] between the adapter flanges.
29-11-81
(a) Make sure that the packings [5] do not get damaged or move out of their positions when
you install the shutoff valve [1].
SUBTASK 29-11-81-420-003
(3) Install the bolts [12], bolt [13], washers [2], and nuts [3].
NOTE: Bolts can be installed from either direction.
SUBTASK 29-11-81-120-001
(4) Clean the contact surfaces of the hinge bracket and bonding jumper [6].
(a) Manually clean the surface of the hinge bracket (TASK 20-10-34-120-801).
1) Use an abrasive pad.
2) Move the pad in a circular movement while you press with your thumb.
3) Final clean the surface.
WARNING
DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH, YOUR EYES, OR
ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM
SOLVENTS. SOLVENTS ARE DANGEROUS MATERIALS.
SOLVENTS CAN BE FLAMMABLE OR CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
ENVIRONMENT . REFER TO THE MATERIAL SAFETY DATA
SHEETS (MSDS) AND THE LOCAL SAFETY PRECAUTIONS.
a) Use a new cotton wiper, G00034 (alternate: knit cotton wiper, G51293),
soaked with solvent, B00062, or solvent, B00184.
b) Rub dry with a clean cotton wiper.
c) Continue to clean and dry the surfaces until the cotton wiper stays clean.
(b) Manually clean the surfaces of the terminal of the bonding jumper [6]
(TASK 20-10-34-110-802).
SUBTASK 29-11-81-390-003
(5) Apply a layer of sealant, A50110, sealant, A50155, sealant, A50231, or sealant, A50296, to the
threads and shank of the bolt [8] used to install the bonding jumper [6].
SUBTASK 29-11-81-390-004
(6) Apply a thin continuous layer of sealant, A50110, sealant, A50155, sealant, A50231, or sealant,
A50296, to the mating surfaces of the bolt [8], washers [2], nut [3], and terminal of the bonding
jumper [6].
SUBTASK 29-11-81-420-013
(7) Install the bolt [8], washers [2], bonding jumper [6], and nut [3].
NOTE: Bolt can be installed from either direction.
NOTE: One washer each under nut, jumper, and bolt head.
SUBTASK 29-11-81-420-014
(8) If it was removed, install the bonding jumper [6] onto the bonding lug of the shutoff valve [1].
(a) Clean the contact surfaces of the bonding lug and bonding jumper [6].
1) Manually clean the surface of the bonding lug (TASK 20-10-34-120-801).
a) Use an abrasive pad.
b) Move the pad in a circular movement while you press with your thumb.
c) Final clean the surface.
29-11-81
WARNING
DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH, YOUR EYES,
OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES
FROM SOLVENTS. SOLVENTS ARE DANGEROUS
MATERIALS. SOLVENTS CAN BE FLAMMABLE OR
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ENVIRONMENT . REFER TO
THE MATERIAL SAFETY DATA SHEETS (MSDS) AND THE
LOCAL SAFETY PRECAUTIONS.
<1> Use a new cotton wiper, G00034 (alternate: knit cotton wiper, G51293),
soaked with solvent, B00062, or solvent, B00184.
<2> Rub dry with a clean cotton wiper.
<3> Continue to clean and dry the surface until the cotton wiper stays clean.
d) If it is necessary, manually apply Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C00862,
to the bonding lug surface.
2) Manually clean the surfaces of the terminal of the bonding jumper [6]
(TASK 20-10-34-110-802).
(b) Install the screw [9], washers [10], bonding jumper [6], and nut [11].
NOTE: Screw can be installed from either direction.
NOTE: One washer each under nut, jumper, and screw head.
(c) Apply sealant, A50110, sealant, A50231, or sealant, A50359, to fully cover the screw [9],
washers [10], terminal of the bonding jumper [6], and nut [11].
SUBTASK 29-11-81-760-001
(9) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the terminal of the bonding jumper [6] and
the following parts (SWPM 20-20-00):
• the hinge bracket
• the bonding lug on the shutoff valve [1] (if it was removed).
(a) Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614.
(b) Make sure that the resistance is not more than 0.001 ohm (1.0 milliohm).
SUBTASK 29-11-81-420-004
(10) Remove the protective cap from the electrical connector [4].
SUBTASK 29-11-81-210-001
(11) Examine the electrical connector [4] for corrosion.
WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES AT AIRPORTS
WHERE DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAIN POTASSIUM FORMATE IS
USED. ALSO DO THE STEPS FOR ALL AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND
CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL
WELL. THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTOR IS PART OF A SYSTEM THAT IS
NECESSARY FOR SAFE FLIGHT .
(a) If there was corrosion, correct the problem (SWPM 20-60-03).
(b) Apply D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171, to the connector (SWPM 20-60-03).
SUBTASK 29-11-81-420-012

29-11-81
(a) Tighten the electrical connector [4] with your hand plus 1/8 turn.
SUBTASK 29-11-81-710-001
(13) Do this task: EDP Supply Shutoff Valve Operational Test, TASK 29-11-81-710-802.
SUBTASK 29-11-81-390-002

D. Reservoir Manual Fill Pump Removal
SUBTASK 29-18-01-860-003
(1) Release the pressure from the reservoirs (TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or
TASK 29-09-00-860-808).
SUBTASK 29-18-01-860-001
(2) Put the reservoir fill selector valve to the CLOSED position.
SUBTASK 29-18-01-020-001
(3) Disconnect the hydraulic line [2] and hydraulic line [5] from the reservoir manual fill pump [1].
SUBTASK 29-18-01-680-001
(4) Drain the hydraulic fluid into a 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154.
SUBTASK 29-18-01-160-001
(5) Clean the working area (TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or TASK 12-40-00-100-803).
SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-001
(6) Install caps on the hydraulic line [2] and hydraulic line [5] to prevent contamination or damage.
SUBTASK 29-18-01-020-006
(7) If the replacement pump does not have unions in the inlet and outlet ports, remove the
union [4], union [7], packing [3], and packing [6].
(a) Discard the packing [3] and packing [6].
29-18-01
SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-002
(8) Install covers on the inlet and outlet ports of the reservoir manual fill pump [1] to prevent
contamination or damage.
SUBTASK 29-18-01-020-002
(9) Remove the bolts [8], washers [9] (under the bolthead), washers [10] (under the nut), and
nuts [11].
SUBTASK 29-18-01-020-003
(10) Remove the reservoir manual fill pump [1].
SUBTASK 29-18-01-020-007
(11) If it is necessary, remove the handle [12] from the reservoir manual fill pump [1].
(a) Remove the bolt [13], washer [14], washer [15], and nut [16].

D. Reservoir Manual Fill Pump Installation
SUBTASK 29-18-01-020-004
(1) Remove the covers from the inlet and outlet ports of the reservoir manual fill pump [1].
SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-007
(2) If the replacement pump does not have unions already installed in the inlet and outlet ports, do
these steps:
(a) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [3], new
packing [6], union [4], and union [7].
(b) Install the packing [6] and union [7] in the inlet port and the packing [3] and union [4] in
the outlet port.
SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-013
(3) If removed, install the handle [12] on the reservoir manual fill pump [1].
(a) Install the bolt [13], washer [14], washer [15], and nut [16].
SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-004
(4) Put the reservoir manual fill pump [1] in its mounting position.
SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-005
(5) Install the reservoir manual fill pump [1] with the bolts [8], washers [9] (under the bolthead),
washers [10] (under the nut), and nuts [11].
SUBTASK 29-18-01-020-005
(6) Remove the caps from the hydraulic line [2] and hydraulic line [5].
SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-006
(7) Connect the hydraulic line [2] to the outlet port of the reservoir manual fill pump [1].
(a) Tighten the B-nut to 170 ±9 in-lb (19 ±1 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-011
(8) Connect the hydraulic line [5] to the inlet port of the reservoir manual fill pump [1].
29-18-01
(a) Tighten the B-nut to 280 ±14 in-lb (32 ±2 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-18-01-420-009
(9) Make sure that there is an adequate separation between tubing, wires and hoses
(TASK 20-10-51-200-801).
(a) If it is necessary, install clamps and spacers to maintain positive separation of wire
bundles from hydraulic tubes (SWPM 20-10-11).
E. Reservoir Manual Fill Pump Installation Test
SUBTASK 29-18-01-610-001
(1) Pump a small quantity of fluid through the reservoir manual fill pump [1]
(TASK 12-12-00-610-801).
SUBTASK 29-18-01-790-001
(2) Examine the reservoir manual fill pump [1] connections for leaks.

A. General
(1) In this procedure, the reservoir fill filter module is referred to as the "filter module", “filter
assembly" and the reservoir fill filter element is referred to as the "filter element".
B. References
Reference Title

(P/B 201)

(P/B 201)

D. Reservoir Fill Filter Module Removal
SUBTASK 29-18-11-860-001
(1) Release pressure from the reservoirs, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization,
TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808.
SUBTASK 29-18-11-020-001
(2) Remove the filter assembly [1].
(a) Put the reservoir fill selector valve to the CLOSED position.
(b) Disconnect the hydraulic line [2] and hydraulic line [5] from the inlet and outlet ports of the
fill filter module head.
(c) Drain hydraulic fluid into a container.
(d) Install caps on the hydraulic line [2] and hydraulic line [5].
(e) Install caps on the unions [4] of the filter head inlet and outlet ports.
(f) If the new filter module does not have unions installed, remove unions [4] and
packings [3].
(g) Discard the packings [3].
(h) Remove the filter module bolts [12] and washers [13].
29-18-11
(i) Remove the reservoir fill filter assembly [1].
(j) If it is necessary, do this task: Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane,
TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the
Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-803.

E. Reservoir Fill Filter Element Installation
RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH FILTER ASSEMBLY FROM PALL AEROPOWER CORPORATION
SUBTASK 29-18-11-420-002
(1) Install the filter element [6].
(a) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [8], new
packing [11], new backup rings [7], new backup ring [10], and to the threads of filter
bowl [9].
(b) Install the packing [11] and the backup ring [10] in the groove in the top end of the filter
element [6].
(c) Install the backup rings [7] and packing [8] in the groove in the filter head.
NOTE: One backup ring goes on each side of the packing.
(d) Install the filter element [6] into the filter head.
(e) Install the filter bowl [9] into the filter head.
(f) Tighten the filter bowl [9] to 62.5 ±12.5 in-lb (7.1 ±1.4 N·m).
(g) Install the MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, between the filter head and filter bowl [9].
CAUTION
PULL DOWN ON THE KNURLED RING OF THE SELF-SEAL
DISCONNECT BEFORE YOU TURN IT . IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS, TOO
MUCH TORQUE WILL BE NECESSARY TO TURN THE RING. THIS WILL
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT .
(h) Reconnect the self-seal (quick) disconnect hose.
RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH FILTER ASSEMBLY FROM PTI TECHNOLOGIES
SUBTASK 29-18-11-420-003
(2) Install the filter element [17].
(a) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [14], new
packing [11], new backup rings [15], new backup ring [16], and to the threads of filter
bowl [18].
(b) Install the packing [11] and the backup ring [16], in the groove in the top end of the filter
element [17].
(c) Install the backup rings [15] and packing [14] in the groove in the filter head.
NOTE: One backup ring goes on each side of the packing.
(d) Install the filter element [17] into the filter head.
(e) Install the filter bowl [18] into the filter head.
(f) Tighten the filter bowl [18] to 62.5 ±12.5 in-lb (7.1 ±1.4 N·m).
(g) Install the MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, between the filter head and filter bowl [18].

D. Reservoir Fill Selector Valve Removal
SUBTASK 29-18-21-020-001
(1) Disconnect the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [15], hydraulic line [10] from the reservoir fill
selector valve [6].
SUBTASK 29-18-21-680-001
(2) Put a container below the reservoir fill selector valve [6] to drain hydraulic fluid.
SUBTASK 29-18-21-160-001
(3) If it is necessary, clean all hydraulic fluid from the installation area.
(a) Do this task: Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces of the Airplane,
TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of the
Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-803.
SUBTASK 29-18-21-420-001
(4) Install the plugs on the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [10], and hydraulic line [15] and caps on
the ports of the reservoir fill selector valve [6].
SUBTASK 29-18-21-020-002
(5) Remove the reservoir fill selector valve [6]:
(a) Remove the nuts [9], washers [8], washers [5], bolts [4], and spacers [7] from the
reservoir fill selector valve [6].
(b) Remove the reservoir fill selector valve [6] from the airplane.
29-18-21
(c) If the new reservoir fill selector valve [6] does not have union [11], union [14], and check
valve [2] installed, do these steps:
1) Remove the union [11], union [14], and check valve [2].
2) Remove and discard the packing [3], packing [12], and packing [13].

E. Reservoir Fill Selector Valve Installation
SUBTASK 29-18-21-420-002
(1) If the check valve, unions, and packings are not installed on the new reservoir fill selector
valve [6], do these steps:
(a) Lubricate the new packing [3], new packing [13], new packing [12], union [14], and
union [11] with MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153.
(b) Remove the caps from the reservoir fill selector valve [6].
(c) Install the check valve [2] and packing [3] on the port of the reservoir fill selector valve [6].
(d) Install the union [14] and packing [13] on the port of the reservoir fill selector valve [6].
(e) Install the union [11] and packing [12] on the port of the reservoir fill selector valve [6].
SUBTASK 29-18-21-420-003
(2) Install the reservoir fill selector valve [6]:
(a) Put the reservoir fill selector valve [6] in its position.
29-18-21
(b) Install the spacers [7], bolts [4], washers [5], washers [8], and nuts [9] that attach the
reservoir fill selector valve [6] to the airplane structure.
SUBTASK 29-18-21-080-001
(3) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [10], and hydraulic line [15].
SUBTASK 29-18-21-420-004
(4) Connect the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [10], and hydraulic line [15] to the reservoir fill
selector valve [6].
SUBTASK 29-18-21-420-007
(5) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [1] to 270 ±14 in-lb (30.5 ±1.6 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-18-21-420-005
(6) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic line [10] and hydraulic line [15] to 170 ±9 in-lb
(19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
F . Reservoir Fill Selector Valve Installation Test
SUBTASK 29-18-21-610-001
(1) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801.
SUBTASK 29-18-21-790-001
(2) Make sure that there is no hydraulic leakage at the reservoir fill selector valve [6].

overhead panel, is on.

control low pressure light system B is on.

1) Make sure that the standby Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) operates.
2) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD LOW PRESSURE light, on the P5 forward
overhead panel, goes off.
3) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward
overhead panel, is on.
4) Move the rudder pedals to the left forward stop and to the right forward stop at a
high rate of 5 cycles and visually check that the rudder surface moves
approximately 27 in. (69 cm) left and right from the neutral position.
NOTE: The visual check can be done from the ground without physical
measurement of the rudder travel.
5) Put in full left pedal and slowly release.
6) Make sure that the rudder pedals are centered.
7) Put in full right pedal and slowly release.
8) Make sure that the rudder pedals are centered.
9) Do a visual check of the rudder control surface, to make sure it is in the
approximate neutral position, within the deadband range of the Standby Rudder
Control Unit (SRCU).
NOTE: The purpose of the visual check is to examine for a large rudder offset from
the neutral position that may result from a failure in the input linkage to the
SRCU. The visual check can be done from the ground without physical
measurement of the position of the rudder surface.
(d) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch to the OFF position.
1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD STBY RUD ON light, on the P5 forward
overhead panel, is off.
2) Make sure that the standby EMDP stops.

2).

pressure is between 1500 psig (105 kg/cm 2) and 1000 psig (70 kg/cm 2).

system.

position.

4. Operational Test of the Standby Hydraulic Actuation System
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) This test makes sure that the standby hydraulic pump and the related indications operate
correctly. This test checks the standby hydraulic pumps low pressure indications through the
system A and system B flight control switches, alternate flaps switch and the auto standby
system relay.

29-21-00
a) Move the rudder pedals to the left forward stop and to the right forward stop at
a high rate for 5 cycles and visually check that the rudder surface moves
approximately 27 in. (69 cm) left and right from the neutral position.
NOTE: The visual check can be done from the ground without physical
measurement of the rudder travel.
b) Put in full left pedal and slowly release.
c) Make sure that the rudder pedals are centered.
d) Put in full right pedal and slowly release.
e) Make sure that the rudder pedals are centered.
f) Do a visual check of the rudder control surface to make sure it is in the
approximate neutral position, within the deadband range of the Standby
Rudder Control Unit (SRCU).
NOTE: The purpose of the visual check is to examine for a large rudder offset
from the neutral position that may result from a failure in the input
linkage to the SRCU. The visual check can be done from the ground
without physical measurement of the position of the rudder surface.

E. Standby Hydraulic EMDP Removal
SUBTASK 29-21-21-020-002
(1) Remove the standby hydraulic EMDP [13].
(a) Remove and discard the lockwire from the electrical connector [12].
(b) Disconnect the electrical connector [12] from the standby hydraulic EMDP [13].
(c) Put a container below the standby hydraulic EMDP [13] to catch hydraulic fluid.
(d) Disconnect the supply line [11], pressure line [10], and case drain line [6] from the
standby hydraulic EMDP [13].
(e) Install caps and plugs on the hydraulic lines and ports.
(f) Remove the bolts [2], bolt [14], washers [1], and washer [15] that attach the standby
hydraulic EMDP [13] to the airplane structure.
(g) Remove the standby hydraulic EMDP [13] from the airplane.
SUBTASK 29-21-21-020-004
(2) If it necessary, remove the reducer [4], reducer [5], and reducer [9].
(a) Remove and discard the packing [3], packing [7], packing [8], and cap ports.
29-21-21
SUBTASK 29-21-21-020-005
(3) Remove the drain plug [18].
(a) If the drain plug [18] P/N AN814-2 was installed, discard it.
(b) If the drain plug [18] P/N 65-13139-2 was installed, keep it.

G. Prepare for the Installation
SUBTASK 29-21-21-960-001
(1) If the hydraulic pump is removed because of a mechanical malfunction of the pump, do these
steps:
NOTE: If the airplane experiences repeated failures of a pump at one location, there could be
debris in the case drain line, case drain hose, or case drain hose quick-disconnect that
cannot be flushed by the accomplishment of this task. Careful
examination/cleaning/replacement of the case drain hose or case drain hose
quick-disconnect could be required.
(a) Examine the case drain line, case drain hose, or case drain hose quick-disconnect for
debris or blockage.
(b) If debris or blockage is found, clean or replace the case drain hose or quick-disconnect,
as applicable.
(c) Inspect the standby case drain filter for metal particle contamination
(TASK 29-21-41-000-801 and TASK 29-21-41-400-801).
SUBTASK 29-21-21-640-001
(2) If the packings, reducers, and drain plug are not installed on the standby hydraulic EMDP [13],
do these steps:
(a) Lubricate the packings and reducers with MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid,
D00153.
(b) Install the new packing [3], reducer [4], new packing [7], reducer [5], new packing [8],
reducer [9], packing [17], and drain plug [18] on the standby hydraulic EMDP [13].
(c) Tighten the reducer [4] to 110 ±6 in-lb (12.4 ±0.7 N·m).
(d) Tighten the reducer [5] to 280 ±14 in-lb (31.6 ±1.6 N·m).
(e) Tighten the reducer [9] to 360 ±18 in-lb (40.7 ±2.0 N·m).
(f) If the drain plug [18] P/N AN814-2 was installed, replace it with the drain plug [18] P/N
65-13139-2.
1) Tighten the drain plug [18] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-21-21-100-001
(3) Clean the bolts [2], bolt [14], washers [1], and contact surfaces (TASK 20-10-34-120-801).
SUBTASK 29-21-21-100-002
(4) Clean the mating surfaces of the standby hydraulic EMDP [13], jumper [16], and washer [15].
29-21-21
(a) Clean the mating surface of the standby hydraulic EMDP [13] with 60 grit or finer wet/dry
aluminum oxide sandpaper, G51464.
1) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist with solvent, B00184, to clean the mating surface
of the standby hydraulic EMDP [13].
2) If it is necessary, use cotton wiper, G00034, to remove remaining solvent.
(b) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist with solvent, B00184, to clean the mating surfaces of
the jumper [16] and washer [15].
SUBTASK 29-21-21-860-004
(5) Fill the standby hydraulic EMDP [13] half full with hydraulic fluid through the supply port.
SUBTASK 29-21-21-110-001
(6) Apply primer, C00259, to all areas of the fastener holes where bolts [2] will be installed
(TASK 51-21-72-370-804).
(a) Let primer, C00259, dry.
H. Standby Hydraulic EMDP Installation
SUBTASK 29-21-21-420-001
(1) Install the standby hydraulic EMDP [13].
(a) Apply sealant, A50110, or sealant, A50155, or sealant, A50296, or sealant, A50231, to
the shank, threads, and under the head of the bolt [14].
(b) Apply sealant, A50110, or sealant, A50155, or sealant, A50296, or sealant, A50231, to
the mating surfaces of the standby hydraulic EMDP [13], washer [15], and jumper [16].
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR-
BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH
WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH
YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL
CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(c) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, to the shank and threads of the bolts [2].
(d) Put the standby hydraulic EMDP [13] in its position.
(e) Install the washers [1], bolts [2], washer [15], bolt [14], and jumper [16] that attach the
standby hydraulic EMDP [13] to the airplane structure.
(f) Make sure that the squeeze-out of sealant is continuous and visible.
(g) Remove the plugs from the standby hydraulic EMDP [13].
(h) Remove the caps from the supply line [11], pressure line [10], and case drain line [6].
(i) Connect the supply line [11], pressure line [10], and case drain line [6] to the standby
hydraulic EMDP [13].
(j) Tighten the supply line [11] to 450 ±23 in-lb (50.8 ±2.6 N·m).
(k) Tighten the pressure line [10] to 270 ±14 in-lb (30.5 ±1.6 N·m).
(l) Tighten the case drain line [6] to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
(m) Connect the supply line for the standby hydraulic system EMDP [13] from the standby
hydraulic reservoir at the quick-disconnect.
NOTE: The quick-disconnect is at the bottom of the standby hydraulic reservoir.
(n) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the standby hydraulic EMDP [13] and
airplane structure (SWPM 20-20-00).
29-21-21
1) Use an non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614.
2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.0010 ohm (1.0 milliohm) or
less.
WARNING
DO NOT GET CHEMICAL CONVERSION COATING SOLUTION IN YOUR
MOUTH, IN YOUR EYES, ON YOUR SKIN, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. DO
NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THIS MATERIAL. AIR MUST FLOW
FREELY THROUGH THE WORK AREA. USE THE NECESSARY
RESPIRATORY PROTECTION. KEEP THIS MATERIAL AWAY FROM
SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . THIS MATERIAL IS POISONOUS AND
FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT .
(o) Manually apply Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C50104, to the bare metal surfaces of
the standby hydraulic EMDP [13] (TASK 51-21-41-370-802).
(p) Remove the cap from the electrical connector [12].
(q) Connect the electrical connector [12] to the standby hydraulic EMDP [13].
(r) Install MS20995C20 lockwire, G50225, on the electrical connector [12]
(TASK 20-10-44-400-801).

(3) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker:

Row Col Number Name

CAUTION

DISCONNECT BEFORE YOU TURN IT . IF YOU DO NOT DO

(1) Lubricate the backup rings [8] and new packing [9] with hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B
fluid, D00054.

damage.
SUBTASK 29-21-41-420-001
(2) Install the backup rings [8] and packing [9] in the filter head.
SUBTASK 29-21-41-640-002
