SUBTASK 29-21-41-640-003
(4) Install the packing [7] in the filter element [10].
SUBTASK 29-21-41-020-004
(5) Put the filter element [10] in the filter bowl [11].
SUBTASK 29-21-41-640-004

D00153.
SUBTASK 29-21-41-980-001

(a) Raise the filter element [10] from the filter bowl [11] and press it onto the filter head.
SUBTASK 29-21-41-020-005
(8) Install the filter bowl [11] on the filter head.
(a) Tighten the filter bowl [11] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 75 in-lb (8.5 N·m).

(9) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, or safety cable kit, G51674, or safety cable kit,

SUBTASK 29-22-00-730-008

WARNING
MAKE SURE PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE SLATS AND

DURING THIS PROCEDURE.
(31) Pressurize hydraulic pressure to system B with the EDP , do this task: Hydraulic System A or B
Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
NOTE: This step makes sure that the system B EDP low pressure switch operates correctly.
The system B EDP must be used to test the EDP low pressure switch and circuit.
SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-044

Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.

Row Col Number Name

SUBTASK 29-22-00-870-001
(34) If it is necessary, move the rudder pedals until the hydraulic pressure in system A and in
system B is less than 200 psig (1379 kPa).
(a) Make sure that the PTU control valve opens.
SUBTASK 29-22-00-860-040
(35) Pressurize hydraulic power to the hydraulic system B with the Electric Motor-Driven Pump
(EMDP) or a ground service cart, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
NOTE: You cannot use the EDP because the EDP pressure switch must indicate low
pressure.
(a) Feel and listen to the PTU to make sure that it does not operate.
(b) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure in system A does not increase.
(c) If the PTU operates or the pressure in hydraulic system A increases, do these steps:
1) Replace the PTU, do these tasks:
• Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Removal, TASK 29-22-11-000-801
• Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Installation, TASK 29-22-11-400-801.
2) Replace the PTU check valve.
3) Replace the PTU pressure filter element, do these tasks:
• PTU Pressure Filter Element - Removal, TASK 29-22-21-020-801
• PTU Pressure Filter Element - Installation, TASK 29-22-21-400-802.

G. PTU Removal
SUBTASK 29-22-11-650-002
(1) Disconnect the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [6], hydraulic line [7], hydraulic line [15],
T-fitting [17], and hydraulic line [21] from the power transfer unit [10].
(a) Put a container below the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [6], hydraulic line [7], hydraulic
line [15], T-fitting [17], and hydraulic line [21] to catch the hydraulic fluid.
(b) Disconnect the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [6], hydraulic line [7], hydraulic line [15],
T-fitting [17], and hydraulic line [21] from the power transfer unit [10].
(c) Install caps on the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [6], hydraulic line [7], hydraulic
line [15], T-fitting [17], and hydraulic line [21].
SUBTASK 29-22-11-650-003
(2) Remove the power transfer unit [10].
(a) Remove the bolts [11] and washers [12] that attach the power transfer unit [10] to the
airplane structure.
(b) Remove the power transfer unit [10].
SUBTASK 29-22-11-020-002
(3) Remove the check valve [24] from the union [2].
SUBTASK 29-22-11-650-004
(4) Remove the union [2], union [5], union [8], union [13], union [16], union [20], and
port-drain [22].
(a) Discard the packing [3], packing [4], packing [9], packing [14], packing [18], packing [19],
and packing [23].
(b) Install the plugs in the hydraulic ports of the power transfer unit [10].

F . Prepare for the Installation
SUBTASK 29-22-11-200-001
(1) If the power transfer unit [10] is replaced because of mechanical malfunction, do these steps:
(a) Replace the power transfer unit [10] pressure filter, do these tasks:
1) PTU Pressure Filter Element - Removal, TASK 29-22-21-020-801.
2) PTU Pressure Filter Element - Installation, TASK 29-22-21-400-802.
29-22-11
(b) Replace the A system return filter, do these tasks:
1) Return Filter Element Removal, TASK 29-11-61-000-801.
2) Return Filter Element Installation, TASK 29-11-61-400-801.
(c) Replace the B system return filter, do these tasks:
1) Return Filter Element Removal, TASK 29-11-61-000-801.
2) Return Filter Element Installation, TASK 29-11-61-400-801.
G. PTU Installation
SUBTASK 29-22-11-640-001
(1) Install the hydraulic fittings in the power transfer unit [10].
(a) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic ports in the power transfer unit [10].
(b) Apply hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B fluid, D00054, to the new packing [3], new
packing [4], new packing [9], new packing [14], new packing [18], new packing [19], and
new packing [23].
(c) Install the packing [3], packing [4], packing [9], packing [14], packing [18], packing [19],
and packing [23], with the union [2], union [5], union [8], union [13], union [16], union [20],
and port-drain [22] in the power transfer unit [10].
1) Tighten the union [2] and union [20] to 99 in-lb (11.2 N·m) - 121 in-lb (13.7 N·m).
2) Tighten the union [8] to 153 in-lb (17.3 N·m) - 187 in-lb (21.1 N·m).
3) Tighten the union [13] and union [16] to 252 in-lb (28.5 N·m) - 308 in-lb (34.8 N·m).
4) Tighten the union [5] to 324 in-lb (36.6 N·m) - 396 in-lb (44.7 N·m).
5) Tighten the port-drain [22] to 99 in-lb (11.2 N·m) - 121 in-lb (13.7 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-22-11-420-003
(2) Install the check valve [24] on the union [2].
SUBTASK 29-22-11-100-001
(3) Fill the power transfer unit [10] (motor and pump) with hydraulic fluid, D00153, until it is
approximately one-half full.
SUBTASK 29-22-11-420-001
CAUTION
INSTALL THE POWER TRANSFER UNIT (PTU) WITH THE MOTOR ON THE
LEFT SIDE OF THE AIRPLANE. IF YOU DO NOT INSTALL THE PTU
CORRECTLY , THE SYSTEM WILL NOT OPERATE.
(4) Install the power transfer unit [10].
(a) Put the power transfer unit [10] in its position in the airplane with the motor on the left
side.
(b) Install the bolts [11] and washers [12] to attach the power transfer unit [10] to the airplane
structure.
(c) Remove the protective caps from the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [6], hydraulic
line [7], hydraulic line [15], T-fitting [17], and hydraulic line [21].
(d) Connect the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [6], hydraulic line [7], hydraulic line [15],
T-fitting [17], and hydraulic line [21] to the power transfer unit [10].
1) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic line [1] and hydraulic line [21] to 256 in-lb
(28.9 N·m) - 284 in-lb (32.1 N·m).
29-22-11
2) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic line [7] and hydraulic line [15] to 475 in-lb
(53.7 N·m) - 525 in-lb (59.3 N·m).
3) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [6] to 427 in-lb (48.2 N·m) - 473 in-lb
(53.4 N·m).
4) Tighten the B-nut on the T-fitting [17] to 280 ±14 in-lb (31.6 ±1.6 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-22-11-610-002
(5) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801.

SUBTASK 29-22-41-420-001
(2) Do these steps to install the pressure switch [1] in the hydraulic system B pressure module:
(a) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist in alcohol, B50262, or alcohol, B00068, to clean the
mating surfaces of the pressure switch [1] and pressure module.
(b) Install the packing [3] on the pressure switch [1].
(c) Remove the plug from the pressure module.
(d) Put the pressure switch [1] in the pressure module.
(e) Tighten the pressure switch [1] to 161 in-lb (18.2 N·m) - 179 in-lb (20.2 N·m).
(f) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the pressure switch [1] and airplane
structure (SWPM 20-20-00).
1) Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614.
29-22-41
2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.0005 ohm (0.50 milliohm) or
less.

G. System Pressure Transmitter Installation
SUBTASK 29-31-12-640-001
(1) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [4] and threads
of the pressure transmitter [1].
SUBTASK 29-31-12-420-001
(2) To install the pressure transmitter [1] for hydraulic system A or B, do these steps:
(a) Install the packing [4] on the pressure transmitter [1].
(b) Install the pressure transmitter [1].

F . Standby System Pressure Transmitter Installation
SUBTASK 29-31-12-420-012
(1) If the packing [11] and union [10] are not installed on the standby system pressure
transmitter [5], do these steps:
(a) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [11] and
union [10].
(b) Install the packing [11] and union [10] on the standby system pressure transmitter [5].
(c) Tighten the union [10] to 126 in-lb (14.2 N·m) - 154 in-lb (17.4 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-31-12-420-011
(2) Do these steps to install the standby system pressure transmitter [5].
(a) Clean the mating surface of the bracket with 60 grit or finer wet/dry aluminum oxide
sandpaper, G51464.
1) Clean the mating surface of the bracket with cotton wiper, G00034, moist in alcohol,
B00130.
(b) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist in alcohol, B00130, to clean the mating surface of the
standby system pressure transmitter [5].
(c) If it is necessary, use cotton wiper, G00034, to remove remaining solvent.
(d) Install the standby system pressure transmitter [5] to the bracket.
(e) Install the nut [8] and washer [9] that attach the standby system pressure transmitter [5].
1) Tighten the nut [8] to 360 ±36 in-lb (41 ±4 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-31-12-760-002
(3) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the standby system pressure transmitter [5]
and bracket.
(a) Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614.

the standby system pressure transmitter [5] and nut [8] with double twist method
(TASK 20-10-44-400-801 or TASK 20-10-44-400-802).
SUBTASK 29-31-12-390-002

2. Case Drain Overheat Switch Test (Preferred Method)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) This test will functionally check the hydraulic system A & B case drain overheat switches and
the associated OVERHEAT lights (ELEC 1 & 2) on the Hydraulic Panel (P5).
(2) With increasing temperature, the overheat switch contacts close at 220 ±5°F (104.4 ±2.8°C).
With decreasing temperature, overheat switch contacts open at minimum 165°F (73.9°C). The
OVERHEAT lights (ELEC 1 & 2) come on when the overheat switches are closed.
B. References
Reference Title
29-32-12-000-801 Hydraulic Fluid Overheat Warning Switch Removal (P/B 401)
29-32-12-400-801 Hydraulic Fluid Overheat Warning Switch Installation (P/B 401)

E. Case Drain Overheat Switch Test (Hydraulic System A)
SUBTASK 29-32-00-020-002
(1) Remove the system A case drain overheat switch (S798). To remove it, do this task: Hydraulic
Fluid Overheat Warning Switch Removal, TASK 29-32-12-000-801.
(a) Make sure that this circuit breaker is open:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3
Row Col Number Name
F 12 C00318 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 6
(b) Reconnect electrical connector D2688 to the overheat switch (S798).
(c) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3
Row Col Number Name
F 12 C00318 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 6
SUBTASK 29-32-00-480-001
(2) Connect the K-Type thermocouple switch tester, SPL-3924, and heater probe BH16440-40 to
the overheat switch.
NOTE: The heater probe BH16440-40 is for use with the hydraulic fluid overheat warning
switches, and is found in the following heater probe kit(s):
TEMPCAL heater probe kit, SPL-3952.
SUBTASK 29-32-00-720-001
(3) Do these steps to functionally check the overheat switch:
NOTE: The following steps should be repeated twice.
(a) Do a check of the overheat switch's actuation "closed" temperature:
1) Stabilize the overheat switch temperature at 220 ±5°F (104.4 ±2.8°C) for a minimum
of two (2) minutes.
2) Slowly increase the overheat switch temperature at a rate of 5+/-1 degrees F/minute
(2.8+/-0.6 degrees C/minute) until the OVERHEAT light (ELEC 2) on the Hydraulic
Panel (P5) comes on.
3) Make a record of the temperature when OVERHEAT light (ELEC 2) came on.
4) Make sure that the overheat switch actuated "closed" at a temperature of 220 ±5°F
(104.4 ±2.8°C) when the OVERHEAT light (ELEC 2) came on.
(b) Do a check of the overheat switch's actuation "open" temperature:
1) Slowly decrease the overheat switch temperature at a rate of 5+/-1 degrees
F/minute (2.8+/-0.6 degrees C/minute) until the OVERHEAT light (ELEC 2) on the
Hydraulic Panel (P5) goes off.
2) Make a record of the temperature when OVERHEAT light (ELEC 2) went off.
29-32-00
3) Make sure that the overheat switch actuated "open" at a temperature no less than
165°F (73.9°C) when the OVERHEAT light (ELEC 2) went off.
(c) Make sure that there is no less than 5 degrees F (2.8 degrees C) of temperature
differential between the recorded temperatures of the overheat switch "closed" and
"open" actuations.
(d) Do each of the above steps a second time.
SUBTASK 29-32-00-080-001
(4) Disconnect the K-Type thermocouple switch tester, SPL-3924, and heater probe BH16440-40
from the overheat switch.
SUBTASK 29-32-00-420-001
(5) Reinstall the system A case drain overheat switch (S798):
(a) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3
Row Col Number Name
F 12 C00318 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 6
(b) Disconnect electrical connector D2688 from overheat switch (S798).
(c) Install the system A case drain overheat switch (S798). To install it, do this task: Hydraulic
Fluid Overheat Warning Switch Installation, TASK 29-32-12-400-801.
(d) Make sure that this circuit breaker is closed:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3
Row Col Number Name
F 12 C00318 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 6

E. Hydraulic Fluid Quantity Transmitter/Indicator Inspection
SUBTASK 29-33-12-860-001
(1) Release pressure from the applicable hydraulic reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs
Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization,
TASK 29-09-00-860-808.
SUBTASK 29-33-12-020-001
(2) Open the drain valve on the bottom of the hydraulic reservoir.
(a) Remove the lockwire or safety cable from the handle of the drain valve.
SUBTASK 29-33-12-680-001
(3) Drain the fluid into a 15 gallon (57 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-6907.
SUBTASK 29-33-12-420-001
(4) Close the drain valve.
SUBTASK 29-33-12-420-002
(5) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51674, on the handle of the
reservoir drain valve with double twist method.
29-33-12
SUBTASK 29-33-12-610-001
(6) Slowly fill the applicable hydraulic reservoir with the fluid quantity specified below, do this task:
Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801.
NOTE: The fluid quantities are correct only if all supply and return lines to the reservoir are
full.
(a) The fluid quantity must be 5.7 gal (21.6 l) for the system A.
(b) The fluid quantity must be 8.2 gal (31.0 l) for the system B.
SUBTASK 29-33-12-210-001
(7) Make sure that the fluid level on the transmitter indicator and the cockpit indicator increases as
you fill the reservoir.
(a) If the fluid level does not increase, refer to the Observed Fault List in the Fault Isolation
Manual (FIM).
SUBTASK 29-33-12-210-002
(8) Make sure that the indicators on the transmitters show full when the system A reservoir is
5.7 gal (21.6 l) and system B reservoir is 8.2 gal (31.0 l).
(a) When the indicators on the reservoir transmitters show full, make sure that the HYD Q %
indicators on the Systems display show 100 +6%/-9%.
(b) If the transmitters and/or the engine display fail to meet these requirements, refer to the
Observed Fault List in the FIM.

SUBTASK 29-33-21-020-001
(5) Drain the standby hydraulic reservoir, do these steps:
CAUTION
PULL DOWN ON THE KNURLED RING OF THE SELF-SEAL
DISCONNECT BEFORE YOU TURN IT . IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS, TOO
MUCH TORQUE WILL BE NECESSARY TO TURN THE RING. THIS WILL
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT .
(a) Disconnect the supply line for the standby hydraulic pump at the quick-disconnect at the
bottom of the standby hydraulic reservoir.
(b) If a spare quick-disconnect hose assembly is available, do the following steps:
1) Put the hose end of the spare quick-disconnect hose assembly into 5 gallon (19

2) Connect the quick-disconnect end of the spare hose assembly to the standby
reservoir.
(c) If a spare quick-disconnect hose is not available, do the following steps:
1) Disconnect the supply hose at the standby hydraulic pump
(TASK 29-21-21-000-801).
2) Put the end of the standby pump supply hose into a 5 gallon (19 liter) container,
STD-1154.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT
BEFORE YOU INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL
DISCONNECT . IF TOO MUCH TORQUE IS NECESSARY ,
DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT , AND MAKE SURE
THAT THE POPPET IS STRAIGHT . AFTER YOU INSTALL IT , MAKE
SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 IN.
(1.52 MM). IF THE INDICATOR PINS ARE NOT CORRECTLY
EXTENDED, FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR STOP . THIS CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE RESERVOIR, AND THE PUMP .
3) Connect the quick-disconnect end of the supply hose to the standby reservoir.
(d) Drain the hydraulic fluid into the 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154.
NOTE: The standby hydraulic reservoir contains approximately 3.6 gal (13.6 l).
29-33-21
SUBTASK 29-33-21-080-002

do these steps:
(a) Remove the spare quick-disconnect hose assembly.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT BEFORE
YOU INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . IF
TOO MUCH TORQUE IS NECESSARY , DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL
DISCONNECT , AND MAKE SURE THAT THE POPPET IS STRAIGHT .
AFTER YOU INSTALL IT , MAKE SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS
EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 IN. (1.52 MM). IF THE INDICATOR PINS
ARE NOT CORRECTLY EXTENDED, FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR
STOP . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE RESERVOIR, AND THE
PUMP .
(b) Connect the supply line for the standby hydraulic pump at the quick-disconnect at the
bottom of the standby hydraulic reservoir.
SUBTASK 29-33-21-080-003
(7) If the supply hose to the standby hydraulic pump was disconnected to drain the standby
reservoir, connect it to the supply port of the pump (TASK 29-21-21-400-801).
SUBTASK 29-33-21-420-007
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE DISCONNECT POPPET IS STRAIGHT BEFORE YOU
INSTALL THE HOSE HALF OF THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT . IF TOO MUCH
TORQUE IS NECESSARY , DISCONNECT THE SELF-SEAL DISCONNECT ,
AND MAKE SURE THAT THE POPPET IS STRAIGHT . AFTER YOU INSTALL IT ,
MAKE SURE THAT THE INDICATOR PINS EXTEND A MINIMUM OF 0.06 IN.
(1.52 MM). IF THE INDICATOR PINS ARE NOT CORRECTLY EXTENDED,
FLUID FLOW WILL DECREASE OR STOP . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
THE RESERVOIR, AND THE PUMP .
(8) Connect the supply line for the standby hydraulic pump at the quick-disconnect at the bottom
of the standby hydraulic reservoir.
SUBTASK 29-33-21-160-001
(9) If you get hydraulic fluid on the airplane, do this task: Clean (Wet Wash) the External Surfaces
of the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or Clean (Waterless Wash) the External Surfaces of
the Airplane, TASK 12-40-00-100-803.

E. Pump Low Pressure Warning System Test for Hydraulic System A or B
SUBTASK 29-34-00-860-002
(1) Set the LIGHTS switch, on the P1 panel, to the TEST position.
SUBTASK 29-34-00-210-001
(2) Make sure that these lights come on:
(a) The two MASTER CAUTION lights (Captain's and First Officer's lightshield)
(b) The HYD light (First Officer's lightshield)
(c) The LOW PRESSURE lights (ENG 1 and ELEC 2 for system A; ELEC 1 and ENG 2 for
system B), on the P5 panel, for the applicable system.
NOTE: Other annunciator lights will come on but you can ignore those lights.
SUBTASK 29-34-00-860-003
(3) Set the LIGHTS switch back to the DIM or BRT position.
SUBTASK 29-34-00-480-001
(4) Install the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163:
NOTE: Do not operate the Engine Driven Pump (EDP)s or Electric Motor-Driven Pump
(EMDP)s with the portable hydraulic cart return and pressure lines connected. This
may prevent the pumps from receiving enough hydraulic fluid from their respective
reservoirs and cavitate the pump.
(a) Disconnect the pressure line from the applicable EDP or EMDP .
(b) Install a cap on the pressure port of the EDP or EMDP .
(c) Connect the pump pressure line to the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163.
(d) Connect the return hose of the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163 to the return port of the
ground service module for the applicable system.
SUBTASK 29-34-00-210-002
(5) Make sure that the applicable LOW PRESSURE lights (ENG 1 and ELEC 2 for system A; ENG
2 and ELEC 1 for system B) come on.
SUBTASK 29-34-00-780-001
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL
CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER.
AILERONS, RUDDER, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SPOILERS, SLATS, AND
THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY
HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT .
(6) Slowly increase the hydraulic pressure.
(a) Make sure that the applicable LOW PRESSURE lights (ENG 1 and ELEC 2 for system A;
ELEC 1 and ENG 2 for system B) go off between 1300 and 1600 psig.
SUBTASK 29-34-00-780-002
(7) Slowly decrease the pressure.
(a) Make sure that the applicable LOW PRESSURE lights (ENG 1 and ELEC 2 for system A;
ELEC 1 and ENG 2 for system B) come on between 1500 and 1200 psig.
29-34-00
SUBTASK 29-34-00-080-001
(8) Remove the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163:
(a) Disconnect the pressure line from the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163.
(b) Remove the cap from the pressure port of the EDP or EMDP .
(c) Connect the pressure line to the pressure port of the applicable EDP or EMDP .
(d) Disconnect the return hose of the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163 from the ground
service module.

G. EMDP Low Pressure Switch Installation Test
SUBTASK 29-34-21-860-008
(1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811.
SUBTASK 29-34-21-710-001
CAUTION
DO NOT OPERATE THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEMS A AND B ELECTRIC MOTOR-
DRIVEN PUMPS FOR MORE THAN TWO MINUTES WITHOUT FUEL IN THE
FUEL TANKS. THE NO. 1 (FOR HYDRAULIC SYSTEM A), AND NO. 2 (FOR
HYDRAULIC SYSTEM B), FUEL TANKS MUST HAVE A MINIMUM OF 250
GALLONS (1675 POUNDS/760 KILOGRAMS) OF FUEL IN THEM. IF THERE IS
NOT SUFFICIENT FUEL IN THE FUEL TANKS, THE ELECTRIC MOTOR-
DRIVEN PUMPS WILL BECOME TOO HOT . THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
THE ELECTRIC MOTOR-DRIVEN PUMPS.
(2) Do the EMDP low pressure switch installation test:
(a) Make sure that the applicable LOW PRESSURE light (ELEC 1 or ELEC 2), on the P5
panel, is on.
NOTE: The ELEC 2 LOW PRESSURE light is for the hydraulic system A EMDP . The
ELEC 1 LOW PRESSURE light is for the hydraulic system B EMDP .
(b) Pressurize the applicable hydraulic system (TASK 29-11-00-860-803).
(c) Put the applicable ELEC (1 or 2) HYD PUMPS switch to the ON position.
1) Make sure that the applicable LOW PRESSURE light (ELEC 1 or ELEC 2) goes off.
(d) Put the applicable ELEC (1 or 2) HYD PUMPS switch to the OFF position.
1) Make sure that the applicable LOW PRESSURE light (ELEC 1 or ELEC 2) comes
on.
SUBTASK 29-34-21-790-001
(3) Make sure that there is no leakage at the applicable EMDP low pressure switch.

F . Standby System EMDP Low Pressure Switch Installation
SUBTASK 29-34-31-640-001
(1) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [4] and new
backup rings [3].
SUBTASK 29-34-31-020-007
(2) Install the packing [4] and backup rings [3] in the low pressure switch [1].
SUBTASK 29-34-31-640-002
(3) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the threads of the low pressure
switch [1].
SUBTASK 29-34-31-020-008
(4) Remove the cap from the standby system pressure module.
SUBTASK 29-34-31-020-009
(5) Install the low pressure switch [1] on the standby system pressure module.
SUBTASK 29-34-31-420-001
(6) Tighten the low pressure switch [1] to 350 in-lb (39.5 N·m) - 375 in-lb (42.4 N·m).
SUBTASK 29-34-31-420-004
(7) Install a lockwire on the low pressure switch [1] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
SUBTASK 29-34-31-420-002
(8) Remove the cap from electrical connector [2].
SUBTASK 29-34-31-420-003
(9) Connect the electrical connector [2] to the low pressure switch [1].
29-34-31

SUBTASK 29-34-31-860-005

TASK 29-09-00-860-801 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-807.
SUBTASK 29-34-31-860-006

Row Col Number Name

E 14 C00316 INDICATOR MASTER DIM SECT 4
SUBTASK 29-34-31-860-007

RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH 'STBY RUD ON' LIGHT ON THE P5-3 PANEL

P5, is on.
RYR ALL
SUBTASK 29-34-31-210-001

SUBTASK 29-34-31-860-008WARNING
WHEN YOU OPEN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS, MAKE SURE THAT THE
OUTER DOOR STAYS AS OPEN AS POSSIBLE. IF THE OUTER DOOR
TURNS IN, THE ATTACHED DOOR COMPONENTS COULD TOUCH THE
INNER DOOR COMPONENTS. THIS CAN CAUSE AN ARC CONDITION
WHEN YOU SUPPLY POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTORS IN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS. BE
CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE
INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS POSSIBLE,
REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST . THE P91 AND P92
PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE
AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES.
